articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Real Madrid vs Betis
articles.standfirst: Sportium te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Real Madrid y al Betis en el Estadio de La Cartuja correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de LaLiga
articles.summary: Sportium te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Real Madrid y al Betis en el Estadio de La Cartuja correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de LaLiga
articles.body: El Real Madrid visita al Betis este viernes en el Estadio de La Cartuja, en el partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de LaLiga 26/27, adelantado por los compromisos europeos de ambos equipos la próxima semana. El conjunto blanco llega al choque en un estado de forma inmejorable. Suma pleno de victorias en las tres primeras jornadas bajo las órdenes de José Mourinho, la última de ellas un contundente 4-0 ante el Málaga en el Santiago Bernabéu, resultado que confirma el gran nivel ofensivo mostrado por el equipo en este arranque liguero. Favorito para el partido entre Real Madrid y Betis Por su parte, el Betis llega a esta cita con las sensaciones muy tocadas. El conjunto de Manuel Pellegrini rompió su buena racha en su último compromiso al caer goleado por 5-2 ante el Levante en el Ciutat de València, un tropiezo que frenó de golpe el buen inicio de temporada verdiblanco y que deja al equipo hispalense en la sexta posición de la tabla, con dos victorias y una derrota en sus tres primeros partidos. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como claro favorito al Real Madrid. Sportium paga la victoria blanca a cuota 1.4, por 5.25 del empate y 6.25 de la victoria del cuadro bético. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes del encuentro. El Betis mostró en su derrota ante el Levante que su defensa arrastra dudas serias, encajando cinco goles en un único partido, mientras que el Real Madrid ha sido un vendaval ofensivo en su última salida, con cuatro tantos ante el Málaga. Sin embargo, el conjunto verdiblanco también dejó patente que es un equipo con argumentos arriba, anotando dos goles pese a la goleada en contra. Con estos datos, según las apuestas deportivas, la probabilidad de que ambos equipos anoten se sitúa por encima de la contraria. Sportium paga a 1.53 el "sí" y a 2.38 el "no". Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con mucho fútbol ofensivo. Tanto el Real Madrid como el Betis han sido protagonistas de encuentros con abundantes goles en su última jornada, sumando entre ambos nueve tantos en sus respectivos partidos. La solidez defensiva no parece ser, precisamente, la nota dominante en ninguno de los dos conjuntos en este arranque de curso. Sportium sitúa la cuota del +2.5 totales a 1.35, por 3 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Real Madrid, con un juego de posesión y ataque continuo por bandas, viene generando un volumen alto de saques de esquina en sus últimos partidos, especialmente en la goleada ante el Málaga. El Betis, por su parte, es un equipo que también busca el juego asociativo y las llegadas por el exterior, aunque su reciente derrota ante el Levante deja entrever que puede verse obligado a asumir un rol más defensivo en esta ocasión, lo que podría reducir su aportación ofensiva en este apartado y elevar el número de córners a favor del conjunto blanco. Sportium paga a 1.65 que se produzcan más de 9 córners y a 2.15 del caso contrario.

articles.title: Hills-Beaver Creek wins big to open 2026 season
articles.summary: ADRIAN, M.N. (KELO) — The top-ranked 9-Man team in Minnesota and defending state champion, the Hills-Beaver Creek Patriots continued their winning ways in 20...
articles.body:
ADRIAN, M.N. (KELO) — The top-ranked 9-Man team in Minnesota and defending state champion, the Hills-Beaver Creek Patriots continued their winning ways in 2026 with a season opening 38-6 victory over Adrian-Ellsworth.

The Patriots got on the board first in this game and made it 8-0 after a successful two-point conversion.

That's when the home team strung together its two best drives of the game. Adrian marched down the entire field, converted a fourth down and even sprinkled a big play in there before capping off the drive with a Jackson Jenniges rushing touchdown.

The Dragons would miss the two-point conversion to trail 8-6, but recovered a surprise onside kick, driving inside the 20 before turning it over on downs.

That's when Hills-Beaver Creek hit a big play of their own and this one went for a score as Brodie Metzger connected with Riggins Rheault for a long touchdown plus two-point conversion to make it 16-6 at half.

Out of the break, the Pats marched down the field again and Metzger would finish it off with his legs, they would go up 24-6 before adding 14 more points in the second half to win this game 38-6.

Up next, Hills-Beaver Creek hosts Renville County West on next Friday, while Adrian travels to Heron Lake-Okabena-Fulda the same day.

articles.title: Colorado upsets Tech 14-13 on blocked field goal
articles.summary: A sloppy game goes Deion’s way
articles.body:
Georgia Tech football had the worst case scenario happen as they begin their season 0-1 after a 14-13 loss to Colorado. Dating back to the Pitt game last season, Tech has won only one game.

After allowing a touchdown with under a minute to go to go down 14-13, Indiana transfer quarterback Alberto Mendoza found Dalen Penson on a 42 yard crosser to put Tech in field goal range and a chance to save the game. Alas, Aidan Birr's 45 yard field goal was blocked before it had a chance to see the sky as time expired.

A line of scrimmage that couldn't hold it's own on either side of the ball

Field goal kicking that was 33% successful

Mental errors creating penalties (9 for 49 yards, but three on PAT attemps)

Uninspired playcalling when needing to kill clock in the redzone

Tech's best moments came on special teams. Tech's lone touchdown came from a 100 yard kickoff return by Rahkeem Smith to tie the game at 7-7 in the second quarter after Colorado's initial score.

Tech for all the hype coming in about the running back room led by Alabama/Michigan transfer Justice Haynes only managed 51 net rushing yards to Colorado's 183 and averaged 1.7 yards/rush. Tech ran only 54 plays to Colorado's 76.

Alberto Mendoza completed 17 of his 23 passes for 237 yards and looked very poised both in the pocket and when scrambilng. He was sacked three times but none of those were on him.

Colorado picked up a couple first downs on their initial drive before Tech stuffed them on a couple runs and forced a Julian Lewis incompletion on 3rd down.

On Tech's first drive with Alberto Mendoza at quarterback, they converted a 3rd & 4 on their first set of downs with a completion to Dalen Penson before Justice Haynes picked up two first downs on the ground. After a short yardage situation was wiped out by a illegal formation penalty and an incompletion, Aidan Birr missed a 30 yard field goal.

Colorado then went three and out, but Tech gave the ball right back on their own 26 from a Jordan Allen fumble on a jet sweep. The Buffs may have had a fumble that was recovered by Tae Harris, but the play was called dead due to forward momentum. On 1st & goal from the 3, the Buffs lost a yard, then lost 7 yards on a bad snap and failed to get in the endzone on 4th & goal from the 3.

Tech took over at the 1 and couldn't get out of their redzone, forcing a punt by Alex Bacchetta that did not go far, giving Colorado short field at Tech's 35. They converted that short field into a five yard Micah Welch touchdown for a 7-0 lead. Tech for no good reason had two offsides penalties on the PAT, but somehow Colorado opted to still kick despite having the ball inside the one yard line.

Thank god that lead lasted next to no time as Rahkeem Smith returned the ensuing kickoff 100 yards to the house. Aidan Birr had to take his PAT 5 yards back because of a false start, but Tech tied it 7-7.

Tech forced Colorado's second punt of the game after a couple set of downs, setting up Tech's first normal drive in what felt like an hour. The rest paid off as Mendoza found Allen, Kevin Roche Jr, Dalen Penson, and Isaiah Fuhrmann all for first downs. On a 3rd & 12, Mendoza extended a play with a ton of scrambling, eventually finding Allen at the four yard line. Tech wasted the short field with a false start on 1st & goal, ending up in a 22-yard Aidan Birr field goal and a 10-7 Tech lead.

Three and outs both ways ended the half.

The second half was putrid for all sides involved. Tech managed one good 30 yard completion to Jordan Allen but punted (and got lucky with a horrible fair catch called at the 5 yard line). Colorado was held just outside of field goal range and punted. Ethan Mackenny then got badly beat on the line to create a third down sack.

Colorado did a CPJ and took up half the quarter on 2-4 yard runs just killing Tech in the trenches. After 9 minutes and a bad snap that killed Colorado's momentum, Kevin Roche Jr. saved Tech's ass blocking Elliott Arnold's 38 yard field goal attempt that would have tied the game up at 10-10 with 7:35 remaining.

Tech followed with the exact drive they needed, a clock burning/run heavy drive that featured a 21 yard completion to Jordan Allen, a third down conversion by Justice Haynes on a toss sweep, and a 3rd & 3 completion to Kevin Roche Jr. to put Tech in the red zone at the two minute warning. Offensive Coordinator George Godsey called very simple runs that got blown up behind the line of scrimmage, letting Colorado use their timeouts and easily hold Tech to a field goal to go up 13-7.

Colorado once again took advantage of Tech's leaky defense, driving easily in a minute and three seconds to take a 14-13 lead.

With 35 seconds left, Tech somehow pulled out half a miracle. Mendoza hit Dalen Penson for 42 yards on first down to get Tech into field goal range. After a couple small plays, Birr had a 45 yard field goal blocked to end the game.

articles.title: 'Encroacher' remark hangs over Yusuf Pathan as former India cricketer turned politician withdraws Gujarat high court appeal over Vadodara land dispute: Case explained
articles.summary: More sports News: The Gujarat High Court on Monday dismissed as withdrawn an appeal filed by former India cricketer and Lok Sabha MP Yusuf Pathan against a single-judge.
articles.body: The Gujarat High Court on Monday dismissed as withdrawn an appeal filed by former India cricketer and Lok Sabha MP Yusuf Pathan against a single-judge order that had described him as an “encroacher” on a piece of government land in Vadodara.Pathan’s lawyer, Shalin Mehta, sought permission to withdraw the plea before a division bench comprising Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal and Justice DN Ray. The lawyer told the court that Pathan’s claim over the land was still being pursued under a state government policy.The division bench subsequently dismissed the appeal as withdrawn.Pathan had challenged land allotment rejectionThe 43-year-old had approached the High Court challenging a single-judge order that upheld the Gujarat government’s decision to reject his request for allotment of the 978-square metre plot owned by the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC).Pathan had claimed the land under a state policy applicable to international cricketers.During an earlier hearing, Pathan had told the court that he was pursuing his claim under a state government scheme and was given four weeks to pursue the matter. The High Court had also warned that he could face higher payment of damages if he took longer to vacate the plot.During Monday’s proceedings, Mehta said they were awaiting a response from the VMC but had not received one.“Because we are saying that there is a circular which allows international cricketers to be given a plot. I think I will withdraw because I haven’t heard anything from them (VMC). I have taken instructions from my client…if it is to happen, it will happen outside the court; otherwise it won’t happen," Mehta submitted.With the appeal withdrawn, Pathan’s attempt to challenge the earlier court order through the division bench has come to an end.VMC had asked Pathan to vacate plotThe dispute dates back to 2024, when the Gujarat government rejected Pathan’s request for allotment of the plot. Despite the rejection, he continued to occupy the land.After Pathan was elected from the Baharampur Lok Sabha seat in West Bengal on a Trinamool Congress (TMC) ticket in 2024, the VMC issued him a notice asking him to vacate the land. Pathan refused and challenged the matter in court.The High Court had previously taken a strong view of his occupation of the plot. During a hearing on June 8, the court came down heavily on Pathan over the alleged “encroachment” and orally questioned how he could enter and occupy the land without completing the required formalities.The matter now moves outside the court as Pathan continues to pursue his claim under the state policy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Los modelos más emblemáticos de Seat: encuentra el que tuvieron tus padres o abuelos
articles.standfirst: El vídeo está realizado con algunos de los modelos más emblemáticos que la marca española guarda en su mítica nave A122 de Zona Franca.
articles.summary: El vídeo está realizado con algunos de los modelos más emblemáticos que la marca española guarda en su mítica nave A122 de Zona Franca.
articles.body: Seat sacó su primer modelo al mercado en 1953. Se trataba de un 1400 y salió de la línea de montaje el 13 de noviembre gracias a una licencia de Fiat, gracias a que la nueva marca española había llegado a un acuerdo con la italiana que le permitía fabricar los modelos transalpinos con el logo español. El coche era de color verde y su diseño tenía mucha inspiración de los modelos americanos de la época. Han pasado de aquello 73 años y desde entonces la historia de Seat nos ha traído modelos memorables sin los cuáles no se podría entender la popularización del automóvil en nuestro país. Mucho se ha hablado en este sentido del 600, lanzado en mayo de 1957 y llamado cariñosamente Pelotilla, Botijo o incluso Ombligo (por aquello de que todo el mundo parecía tener uno). Al pequeño Seat le correspondió el honor de ser el primer coche para decenas de miles de familias que por primera vez tenían autonomía par ir a trabajar o desplazarse a la playa, sin importar que detrás viajaran dos, tres o incluso cuatro hijos. En total se vendieron casi 800.000 unidades del pequeño 600, lo que supuso un éxito espectacular. Pero la lista de sus modelos más emblemáticos es muy extensa e incluye modelos irrepetibles como los Seat 850 (tuvo hasta una versión descapotable), 124, 1430, 127, Ritmo, Panda (uno de los coches que mejor apreciados por su icónico diseño), Ibiza (un auténtico súper ventas), Toledo, León, Ateca... Todos ellos quedaron inmortalizados en un vídeo producido con los modelos que la marca guarda en su Nave A122 de Zona Franca, con los que los aficionados esperan que algún día la marca hispana conforme un museo abierto al público. Y entre ellos seguro que está aquel que tuvieron tus abuelos o tus padres, o bien aquél con el que tú mismo aprendiste a conducir o aún llevas a diario. Precisamente porque muchos hemos visto en la familia algún Seat a lo largo de nuestras vidas, la noticia sacada por un medio alemán sobre una hipotética desaparición (sobre la que al final el Grupo Volkswagen no ha tomado ninguna decisión en su Consejo de Vigilancia) trasciende lo puramente económico para afectarnos en lo emocional.

articles.title: Massimo Benassi enfría la euforia del Deportivo: “Ahora mismo en nuestras cabezas quedan 40 puntos”
articles.standfirst: El CEO del Deportivo de A Coruña defendió en 'La Tribu' la estabilidad del proyecto, la planificación del mercado y el objetivo de consolidarse en Primera paso a paso
articles.summary: El CEO del Deportivo de A Coruña defendió en 'La Tribu' la estabilidad del proyecto, la planificación del mercado y el objetivo de consolidarse en Primera paso a paso
articles.body: Massimo Benassi pasó por La Tribu en pleno regreso del Deportivo de A Coruña a Primera División. El CEO blanquiazul analizó el momento del club, la ilusión que se respira en la ciudad y el proyecto que lidera Juan Carlos Escotet desde los despachos. Todo ello con un mensaje de prudencia por encima de cualquier entusiasmo: el objetivo sigue siendo la permanencia. “El Deportivo ahora está muy bien”, reconoció Benassi, aunque quiso mirar más allá del escaparate actual. El dirigente recordó que el club inició en 2023 un trabajo profundo de saneamiento financiero y que la salida del concurso de acreedores fue “el hito más grande” de todo este proceso. “Somos los mismos que estábamos en Primera RFEF en 2023 y nunca se nos va a olvidar de dónde venimos”, afirmó. Benassi rebajó cualquier tentación de mirar demasiado lejos. Preguntado por la dificultad de mantenerse en Primera, el CEO del Deportivo admitió que la temporada será “muy complicada” por el nivel y la competitividad de LaLiga, pero defendió el mismo discurso que ha acompañado al club desde su llegada: “El partido a partido y el semana a semana”. La idea se repitió cuando se puso sobre la mesa la posibilidad de hablar de Europa. “No nos vamos a salir de nuestro discurso y de nuestro objetivo”, insistió. El Deportivo no quiere perder el foco pese al buen arranque, la ilusión del entorno y la ambición que rodea al proyecto. “Ahora mismo en nuestras cabezas quedan 40 puntos y eso es lo que vamos a pelear”, resumió. El CEO explicó también cómo ha podido el Deportivo firmar un mercado tan potente en su regreso a la máxima categoría. Benassi habló de una palabra clave: planificación. Según detalló, el club tenía preparados diferentes escenarios y terminó ejecutando el que le permitió mantener a los jugadores que quería retener y firmar a los futbolistas que tenía marcados. Benassi defendió que el Deportivo ha trabajado dentro del control económico de LaLiga y que la salida del concurso de acreedores fue fundamental para afrontar este verano con margen. También destacó el apoyo del presidente Escotet, al que señaló como pieza esencial para dotar al club de estabilidad y solvencia en esta nueva etapa. Más allá del mercado, Benassi quiso subrayar que el Deportivo no pretende vivir solo del impulso del ascenso. El dirigente explicó que el club ha realizado inversiones importantes en instalaciones, en la ciudad deportiva y en el estadio, además de estar terminando un nuevo edificio para el primer equipo y el filial. Para el CEO, esa apuesta es clave a la hora de convencer a futbolistas. “El jugador también percibe que esto no es un proyecto que va de corto plazo solo y es un proyecto que va de medio a largo plazo”, aseguró. En esa línea, defendió que los jugadores entienden la ambición del Deportivo y quieren formar parte de ella. La entrevista también dejó detalles del cierre de mercado. Benassi explicó cómo se gestaron las llegadas de Josema Giménez y Marc Casadó, dos operaciones de último día que el Deportivo trabajó con antelación mediante llamadas, posicionamiento y contacto constante con los agentes. El CEO reconoció que, en otro momento del mercado, esas incorporaciones habrían sido “totalmente imposibles” desde el punto de vista económico. La clave estuvo en estar atentos al último día y en la voluntad de los futbolistas: “En cuanto los jugadores nos dieron el OK, ya fue un trabajo de todo el equipo fuera del campo”. Benassi reveló que el club consiguió inscribir a los dos “en los últimos 10 minutos”. Benassi también habló de la identidad del Deportivo y de su vínculo con A Coruña. El CEO reconoció que una de las cosas que más le impactó al llegar fue comprobar que en la ciudad “solo existe el Depor”. Para él, esa conexión con la gente es una de las grandes fortalezas del club y algo que debe seguir potenciándose. Sobre el regreso del derbi gallego en Primera, evitó entrar en comparaciones con el Celta y prefirió ampliar el foco. “Para el fútbol de Galicia y para el fútbol español es una magnífica noticia que se pueda volver a dar el derbi en Primera División”, señaló. El Deportivo vuelve a la élite con ambición, pero también con un mensaje muy claro desde los despachos: primero, los 40 puntos.

articles.title: Óvulos congelados: ¿Opción o peaje?
articles.standfirst: Más allá del deporte profesional, se trata de la conciliación entre maternidad y vida laboral
articles.summary: Más allá del deporte profesional, se trata de la conciliación entre maternidad y vida laboral
articles.body: Me da un poco de reparo opinar sobre el tema de la congelación de óvulos de las futbolistas internacionales por mi condición masculina, pero dado que en el fondo se trata de un asunto laboral y servidor de ustedes es un trabajador, entraremos en el tema. Y diremos que no se pueden dejar de lado las críticas de Ana Peleteiro o de Ona Carbonell a la medida, ni descalificarlas aludiendo a posiciones previas. No vamos a entrar en si la medida es machista o no o si parte, como así es, de una petición de las propias jugadoras a su 'empresa', la Real Federación Española de Fútbol. No podemos olvidar tampoco que las carreras en el deporte profesional, para hombres o mujeres, son relativamente breves y en gran parte dependientes de mantener un estado físico óptimo. Pero tampoco podemos ignorar que esta medida se acerca sospechosamente a la consideración de la maternidad como una 'enfermedad', y que llega en un momento en que de forma igualmente sospechosa, desde muchos ámbitos se asocian las bajas médicas al absentismo laboral mientras se clama por el coste que esto supone a empresas, empleadores, etcétera. En realidad, de lo que se está hablando es de si las mujeres pueden decidir tener a sus hijos cuando ellas quieran, o se deberá ajustar el calendario reproductivo a intereses económicos o si, de nuevo, ser madre penaliza y es mejor que no se sea mientras se trabaja. Nada que decir cuando la decisión es personal, pero Ana Peleteiro se pregunta por dos cosas: por alternativas para la conciliación de forma que ser madre no penalice profesionalmente -y eso vale para deportistas de élite y para trabajadoras 'normales'- y por qué pasará cuando esta posibilidad sea una 'expectativa', suponemos que de aceptación, de las pacientes. Luego, el empleador puede ofrecer el servicio... o no ofrecerlo y que cada cual se apañe. ¿Llegaremos a ver en el mercado laboral 'normal', a jubiladas de 65 años -o lo que sea en su momento- como madres de óvulos congelados a los 25? Es un argumento que no se les ocurrió a Isaac Asimov, Stanislaw Lem o a Pohl y Kornbluth, pero quién sabe si en algún momento dejará de ser ciencia ficción para convertirse en costumbrismo...

articles.title: "Cuando empecé éramos 10 mujeres ciclistas federadas y aquí estoy en Vietnam con mis 79 años"
articles.standfirst: Pilar Sanguino, la más veterana del Desafío Santalucia, lleva 46 años sin parar dando pedaladas por carreteras y caminos
articles.summary: Pilar Sanguino, la más veterana del Desafío Santalucia, lleva 46 años sin parar dando pedaladas por carreteras y caminos
articles.body: Estamos en Phong Nha, el Parque Nacional Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng, un paraíso para los más aventureros por ser un impresionante destino de cuevas y selva situado en la provincia de Quảng Bình, en el centro de Vietnam. Atrás quedan tres duras etapas ciclistas entre montañas y arrozales en la zona de Mai Chau. Llegamos después de una noche en tren que sirve para repasar con Pilar lo que han sido estos primeros días del Desafío Santalucia. A sus 79 años es la única mujer de los cinco candidatos elegidos para esta edición en Vietnam y la que tiene una historia más larga ligada a la bicicleta después de 46 años en el Club Ciclista Pueblo Nuevo. "Cuando yo empecé con el ciclismo hace 46 años apenas éramos diez mujeres federadas. Te miraban raro, pero yo no he dejado de hacerlo y aquí sigo, en Vietnam dándolo todo con mis 79 años", nos cuenta Pilar, que dedica cuatro días semanales a hacer montaña y bici para mantenerse en forma. Se le nota a Pilar que el cansancio ha hecho mella en su cuerpo después de tres etapas ciclistas y mucho desnivel en sus piernas: "El tercer día ha sido el peor para mí porque no me he encontrado nada bien, sobre todo al inicio de la etapa, pero gracias a mis compañeros he ido a más y hemos podido acabarla todos". Pilar se siente afortunada y orgullosa de sí misma por ser la única mujer y la más veterana del Desafío Santalucia. "Hay que dejar el sofá y la televisión y conectar con la naturaleza y el deporte como estilo de vida. Te sientes mucho mejor". Y no hay obstáculos que detengan a Pilar en el camino. Hace menos de un año tuvo una lesión grave con rotura de peroné y maleolo, pero seis meses después se volvió a subir a una bici: "Me da igual lo que digan, yo voy a seguir hacia adelante. Por eso cuando acabe el Desafío, el siguiente objetivo será irme a Nepal". Pero antes debe afrontar momentos únicos como los que le quedan por vivir estos próximos días en Vietnam: "Ahora vamos a disfrutar del rápel, de la espeleología, del paddle SUP, del trekking...", dice Pilar. Phong Nha es el corazón de la aventura. Y es lo que toca en los tres próximos días del Desafío Santalucia. Aquí la tierra ha sido esculpida durante millones de años por el agua y aquí se encuentran algunas de las cuevas más grandes y espectaculares del planeta. Llega el momento más exigente del Desafío: jornadas de trekking por la selva, espeleología, rápel y paddle SUP se sucederán en un escenario tan salvaje como fascinante. El esfuerzo tendrá además una recompensa extraordinaria: pasar la noche en el interior de las propias cuevas, bajo gigantescas bóvedas de roca que llegan a alcanzar los 150 metros de altura.

articles.title: Pablo Cardona: "No pongo fecha a mi vuelta, estoy en un punto complicado"
articles.standfirst: El extremeño, que lleva sin jugar desde abril por sus problemas en la rodilla, charló con MARCA durante el Comunidad de Madrid Premier Padel P1
articles.summary: El extremeño, que lleva sin jugar desde abril por sus problemas en la rodilla, charló con MARCA durante el Comunidad de Madrid Premier Padel P1
articles.body: Una de las grandes sorpresas del Comunidad de Madrid Premier Padel P1 fue la presencia de Pablo Cardona. El jugador extremeño, de baja indefinida por lesión en la rodilla desde el pasado mes de abril, estuvo presente en el acto en el que la marca que le viste, Bullpadel, presentaba su nueva gama de palas. Entre ellas, la suya. El zurdo, que sigue inmerso en el proceso de recuperación y que tuvo que volver a parar tras perderse el tramo final de 2025, volver al lado de Javi Leal y recaer, atendió a MARCA Pádel unos minutos y nos contó sus sensaciones y plazos estimados para su vuelta a las pistas. La pregunta, por tanto, era inevitable: ¿Cuándo volverá Pablo Cardona? El de Mérida, esta vez, prefiere no ponerse plazos. "Me encantaría responderte que mañana, pero de momento va a haber que esperar. No pongo fecha. Ya me equivoqué la primera vez que volví y ahora, sin fecha, con calma y haciendo las cosas bien", explica. Cardona reconoce que los últimos meses no están siendo sencillos. "Estoy en un punto complicado, la verdad. Estuve bastante jodido después de volver a parar", admite. Sin embargo, el jugador ya empieza a ver la luz al final del túnel. "Ahora estoy mejor, puedo hacer vida normal, al menos. Estoy trabajando mucho, haciendo mucha rehabilitación, poniéndome fuerte otra vez y haciéndome muchas pruebas, sobre todo para tenerlo todo bien controlado y que no se nos escape nada", añade. El parón por lesión también le ha obligado a tomar cierta distancia del circuito. Estar presente en los torneos, pero sentirse todavía lejos de la competición, no resulta sencillo para un jugador que llevaba años instalado en la élite. "Me cuesta venir a los torneos. No veo nada, no sigo la actualidad del pádel", reconoce. Su manera de mantenerse vinculado a este deporte pasa ahora por echar la vista atrás: "Veo muchos partidos antiguos, estudio lo que puedo con Nerone e intento analizar mis partidos de antes. Pero de la actualidad estoy completamente desconectado porque me cuesta verme fuera de esto". Pese a todo, Cardona transmite tranquilidad y confianza en el proceso. "Estoy poniendo todo de mi parte, mi equipo está trabajando muchísimo y creo que estoy en manos inmejorables", asegura. Y lanza un mensaje de optimismo de cara a su regreso: "Estoy seguro de que antes de que nos demos cuenta estaré otra vez a tope, disfrutando y ganando partidos otra vez". Lo que sí tiene claro es que no quiere volver a cometer los mismos errores. Su anterior regreso estuvo marcado por la intención de recuperar sensaciones mientras competía, pero el cuerpo terminó diciendo basta. "Yo volví con la idea de seguir recuperándome mientras competía. Todavía no estaba al 100%, me faltaba un poquito, entonces la idea fue empezar a ir rodándome", recuerda. Pero el proceso de recuperación, en su opinión, requiere respetar todos los pasos: "Al final de la recuperación, para los que hayan tenido alguna, tú empiezas entrenando un día, luego entrenas tres días, otra semana buscas entrenar cinco días y luego buscas competir. Creo que me salté algún que otro paso y, cuando volví a meter carga de competición, no aguanté ni la competición ni los entrenamientos". La conclusión fue clara: parar de nuevo y empezar de cero. "Aquí, sin estar al 100%, no le ganas a nadie. Yo vivo de mi físico, sin mi potencia no destaco. Entonces decidí parar, recuperarme y cuando esté al 100% volveré", sentencia. Ahora, toca paciencia. Cardona no quiere repetir los errores del pasado ni precipitar un regreso que pueda volver a llevarle al punto de partida. Mientras tanto, seguirá trabajando lejos de los focos. "Hasta entonces estaré trabajando en la sombra". Y, preguntado con una sonrisa por si habrá que esperar hasta 2027 para volver a verle en pista, el extremeño se mostró confiado: "Sí, 2027 creo que toca".

articles.title: ESPN risks all of its anti-woke progress by rehiring controversial host Stan Verrett
articles.summary: ESPN rehired Stan Verrett for NFL Network despite his history of divisive social media posts, raising questions about Burke Magnus' editorial standards.
articles.body: The perception in and around ESPN is that management has tried to distance itself from the divisive, political rhetoric that defined the network over the past decade. Executive vice president Burke Magnus has led the effort. Magnus has elevated personalities who provide a more positive, fan-focused perspective on sports, from Pat McAfee and Peter Schrager to Josh Pate and Jason McCourty. The network parted ways with several commentators and declined to renew the contracts of others who frequently generated headlines for comments critics considered toxic or political, including Ryan Clark, Mark Jones, Clinton Yates, Sarah Spain and Max Kellerman. Magnus's actions sent a message to current and future employees. Self-serving commentary and social media activity that undermine the company's reputation are no longer tolerated. Viewers have noticed. Nearly every one of ESPN’s daily studio shows has gained viewership year over year. For that, Magnus deserves credit. DAN LE BATARD THINKS THERE ARE TOO MANY WHITE NFL ANALYSTS, DESPITE THE RACIAL MAKEUP OF HIS OWN COMPANY And yet, his latest decision undermines his own edict, suggesting to employees that the very behavior he has spent the past two years eliminating is again welcome. On Thursday, ESPN announced that it had rehired Stan Verrett to host a daily show on its sister network, NFL Network. Sources tell OutKick that Magnus and executive Mike McQuade chose Verrett for the role. The move is notable because ESPN did not renew Verrett’s contract last year. Verrett claimed the departure was his decision. Sources have told OutKick otherwise. Either way, ESPN is bringing him back despite knowing how he conducted himself during his previous tenure. Perhaps no recent ESPN employee behaved less professionally on social media than Verrett. We would know. For years, Verrett tweeted obsessively about us, predicted our demise, denounced us as racist, and directly messaged me "f--- you" after following me. Some of those posts are below: Below is a friendly back-and-forth between SportsCenter anchor Nicole Briscoe and me about President Trump. Verrett inserted himself into the mentions by spreading unprompted racial hysteria. "I can help here, Nicole. [Burack] works for a site [OutKick] that uses some of the same kind of racially-tinged rhetoric to attract a specific audience to try to get them to gamble. Plausible deniability is the escape hatch for all the foolishness." Huh? It wasn't just us. Verrett spent much of his final years at ESPN picking social media fights with people who voiced even mildly conservative opinions. In many cases, he dismissed arguments he disliked as — wait for it — racist. Verrett told former college football player T.J. Moe that white people like him have "every advantage available in this society" because Moe rejected the idea that white moviegoers care about the skin color of performers. "No, Black people support other Black people because if we didn’t, history tells us they might not get any support at all. We know you’re not going to do it, based on your whining. Quit tying so hard to be a victim. You have every advantage available in this society." Verrett’s sports commentary isn’t much different. ESPN is privately dissatisfied with its WNBA coverage, particularly the negative tone and racial emphasis some of its commentators have attached to the league. Verrett is unlikely to help address those concerns. He recently got into a spat with an anonymous account with roughly 150 followers, arguing that biases help explain Caitlin Clark’s popularity among white people and Middle America. "If you worry about people thinking you’re racist for supporting Clark, that’s between you and your mirror. Rational, honest people understand that a part of her appeal is to middle America, particularly white people in middle America. And that’s fine. But people lie and pretend it has nothing to do with it ..." Perhaps Magnus forgot when he re-hired Verrett that white people and Middle Americans watch sports, too. Verrett also regularly seeks responses from Dave Portnoy, Clay Travis, Jason Whitlock and Megyn Kelly, reminding viewers of his contempt for prominent figures who represent the views of roughly half the country. Notably, he took issue with one of Travis’ posts advocating against transgender athletes competing in female sports: So, the question is why. Why would Magnus and McQuade hire Verrett back? ESPN has younger anchors on its roster. It could have used NFL Network, which draws fewer than 100,000 viewers in most time slots, as a proving ground for up-and-coming talent. Instead, it turned to Verrett, a 60-year-old anchor who is significantly older than the channel’s average viewer." It’s difficult to see the upside in hiring someone with such a documented history of alienating a substantial portion of the country. His public persona runs directly counter to ESPN’s stated preference for avoiding unnecessary conflict. OutKick asked ESPN on Thursday why it hired Verrett. The network did not provide a clear response. However, the timing raises questions about whether recent criticism of Magnus influenced the decision. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Last month, OutKick first reported that ESPN was laying off Ryan Clark. After Clark’s dismissal, the influential radio show "The Breakfast Club" claimed that Magnus leaked the information to OutKick to embarrass Clark by having him fired in the middle of his show. To be clear, Magnus was not our source. It's unclear why ESPN informed Clark of his exit during a commercial break of "NFL Live," after learning OutKick planned to report it later in the day. Later that week, Clark repeatedly described Magnus on his podcast as the executive who did not like him and suggested Magnus may have had a problem with "how black" Clark says he was. "I couldn’t be too black [at ESPN]," Clark said. Clark offered no evidence that Magnus’ decision was motivated by race. More plausible explanations for why ESPN dismissed him include Clark’s on-air belittling of colleague Peter Schrager, his criticism of Robert Griffin III’s marriage to a white woman, and his retraction of unsupported claims about Louisiana law enforcement officers. Nonetheless, Clark’s comments created a narrative among certain audiences, including The Breakfast Club, Threads and Bluesky. Such accusations, while unsupported, undoubtedly place Magnus, a top Disney executive, in an uncomfortable position. For years, we’ve watched executives respond to similarly unfounded allegations of racism by making decisions intended to demonstrate that the allegations are untrue. Rehiring Stan Verrett, who had employed much of the same racial rhetoric as Clark, could help Magnus refute that narrative. Interestingly, Jemele Hill said on YouTube that Clark spent time with her and Verrett after leaving ESPN. We asked ESPN whether the criticism of Magnus played any role in the decision to bring back Verrett. We did not receive a response. In any event, Magnus weakened the standard he set by hiring Verrett. Notice that ESPN had not generated its usual wave of negative headlines for veering away from sports in recent months. Magnus had almost entirely eradicated the type of commentary that divided fans along political and racial lines. Ryan Clark's firing confirmed Magnus's vision. Employees received the message. Yet, by rehiring Stan Verrett, employees will naturally wonder whether fighting on X and reflexively accusing critics of racism is back in style. How could they not? The addition is disappointing for sports fans. NFL Network was created for football fans of all demographics. Now, the channel is showcasing someone with a documented history of expressing hostility toward a significant portion of that audience. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Burke Magnus deserves credit for the improved state of ESPN. That's on him. He also deserves scrutiny for this decision, one that could undermine the culture he worked so hard to improve.

articles.title: John Cena on His Heel Turn, WWE Retirement, Gunther and What He Doesn't Miss
articles.summary: Even in his retirement from the ring, the grind hasn't stopped for John Cena.
articles.body:
Even in his retirement from the ring, the grind hasn't stopped for John Cena.

The record-setting 17-time world champion did big business for WWE in 2025, his final year as an active competitor. He headlined a plethora of premium live events including Royal Rumble, SummerSlam and WrestleMania, captured championships and tried his hand at turning heel.

After tapping out to Gunther in his final-ever outing last December, Cena quickly and seamlessly transitioned into his new role as an ambassador for WWE, going on to appear at WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas as the official host of the event and announcing the inaugural John Cena Classic at Backlash.

Away from wrestling, he's simultaneously spending his time taking on more acting projects and playing Clash of Clans.

Keeping Busy in Retirement and What He Misses About Wrestling

Cena has long been an avid player of the popular app game with over two billion lifetime downloads, making his involvement in the Search for Cena campaign all the more rewarding.

"Promotions like this to me are the sweet spot," Cena exclusively told Bleacher Report. "Whenever a company comes to you and says, 'Hey, we kind of want to do this thing based off of the You Can't See Me, but we heard that you might be also into the game...' And then you sit down and talk with them and the folks at Supercell gather information together that puts forth an authentic story as to why we're doing it."

The Search for Cena will see "Barbarian King" Cody Rhodes recruit the rest of the WWE Superstars available to play as in the game (The Undertaker, IYO SKY and Jey Uso, among others) and everyone else in the Clash community to hunt down the Cenation Leader between Sept. 1 and Sept. 15.

A one-time-only statue of The American Nightmare awaits those who manage to locate Cena's base.

Cena and Rhodes are rekindling their rivalry in the virtual world in the wake of their Undisputed WWE Championship wars in 2025 and their early encounters in the game many years ago.

"I think it's kind of built for us over at WWE, especially when we got into it," Cena said about using Clash of Clans to pass the time while traveling for WWE. "You were on the road far more than you were home, and the way that they set up making your clan and being able to have people participate was just kind of a way for me to stay interactive with the guys.

"It was just a way for us to have that camaraderie," he continued. "Weirdly enough, before Clash, all the boys used to play cards and cards like kind of fell by the wayside with the generation that I came up with. I would even say with The Hardy Boyz and then with like the OVW class, it kind of fell by the wayside. Clash became the new conduit for busting each other's chops and conversation just for us to stay friends."

That camaraderie among the guys and girls in the locker room is among the many things Cena misses most about being a full-time talent in WWE. Of course, nothing compares to the adrenaline rush of competing in front of thousands and that instant sense of gratification, especially compared to the tedious nature of the acting realm.

One would assume that the hectic travel required of the wrestlers is what Cena doesn't miss about the business, but it's actually everything he endured from a physical standpoint, simply because his body couldn't endure it any longer by the time he hung up his boots for good.

"I like that life, I like the fraternity, I love the ever-changing live audience," Cena said. "The narrative is, like, I can waste all your interview time telling you how much I love it and how much I miss all of that stuff. So, one shining guideline was, physically, I'm older. I'm slower. My sprint time is down. My vertical jump is down. My strength is down.

"How many red flags, how many lights on the dash have to go on before you say like, 'Hey, it's time to move on'? I still have my health. I still feel very good. But honestly, if it if I was bulletproof, I'd still be in there with the guys."

Despite calling it quits last December, the Coyote vs. Acme star showed signs of "Super Cena" in the twilight of his iconic career. His critically-acclaimed wars with Rhodes, CM Punk and AJ Styles proved he had a little left in the tank than he initially let on.

For years, Cena maintained that he would wrap it up once he felt he could no longer deliver at an elite level consistently, and true to his word, he did just that, but only after holding a year-long retirement tour that featured a slew of milestone moments and moments.

In addition to saying farewell to his fans around the world, he did things that had long eluded him—the heel turn being chief among them.

Cena previously portrayed a villain at the onset of his WWE main roster run, but never while he was wrestling on top. That was what made his turn at Elimination Chamber 2026 so shocking and so satisfying.

Unfortunately, the fallout left a lot to be desired, at least creatively. There were glimmers of greatness during his heel run, but by and large, it wasn't what fans always envisioned it would be.

Cena has never been one to entertain "what if?" scenarios. He famously refused to reveal what the original plan was for his heel pairing with The Rock during an appearance on Insight with Chris Van Vliet and what it would have looked like had Rock and Travis Scott stuck around after WrestleMania 41.

When asked about whether he feels his Hall of Fame-worthy career would have been incomplete had he not gone through with that ill-fated heel turn last year, Cena responded with a rather insightful answer analyzing what about it worked and what didn't.

"That's a great question," he told B/R. "A hypothetical one, but I'll walk down a hypothetical lane. Let's say we never do it. I think that would give you as a writer, great canon for articles to write on, like, 'Man, what would it have been like?' But now we have what really happened. We got a heel version of me and we did the best we could with the time we had. And as far as, like, did it work or not? Okay, there's a lot of aspects to that from a business side.

"We didn't have a seat left," Cena continued. "And, you know, people watched in numbers. So, I don't know if it didn't work from a business standpoint. But then there's the creative standpoint. Sometimes blockbuster movies are poorly reviewed by critics. So, I understand where critically people are, like, 'Man, that's just not what I wanted to see.'"

Cena added that he would have loved to have had a chance to "literally ruin wrestling," to wrestle so poorly that people would have wanted him to go for good and to see a hero rise up to oppose him. He affirmed that they didn't have that kind of time, and that it wouldn't have been good for business.

He's also accountable for the critique. As seen on Netflix's WWE Unreal behind-the-scenes series, plans are constantly changing in WWE, and plans certainly changed with Cena's heel turn at at almost every turn. All in all, though, he has no regrets.

"I guess long and short, I'm glad to have done it," Cena said. "I never asked for it. It wasn't my idea. It was Paul's [Triple H] idea. And he even said himself, he asked me and in two seconds, it was a yes. Just like facing Brock or against Gunther. That's how I do business. Just let me tell the story my way. You know? So, if we never did it, I would have been fine. And it would have been nice for you guys to write about, 'Oh, man, he never did it.' In reflecting, I wouldn't change a thing."

Cena feels the lessons learned from the heel turn can be taught to the younger talent, specifically with how to be bold and take chances. He understands that some fans will see that run as a failure, but he's proud to have swung boldly.

The same can be said about his last match with Gunther at Saturday Night's Main Event in December. The bout itself was undoubtedly excellent, but Cena going against his "Never Give Up" mantra by tapping out to Gunther caused quite the stir among fans online.

An argument was made in the moment that Gunther would benefit big time from submitting Cena in unprecedented fashion, and he definitely did in the first few months thereafter.

With The Ring General having cooled off considerably since then, fans now wonder if it was worth it.

While addressing Gunther's status and how WWE has followed up with him, Cena discussed talent frustration and how he personally dealt with it at various points during his time on top.

"Everyone in the locker room at one point gets to a point of frustration," he told B/R. "I gotta be honest with you: Over my 23 years, I might've had two or three moments of fleeting frustration. They were, like, the blink of an eye because I always loved what I did... You didn't see me complain. I know there's a lot of reports and everybody talks about backstage drama. There was never a 'John Cena's frustrated with management' [report] because it's just not true. Not believable. I know there's frustration in all towns of like, 'Yo, man, I just did this spectacular thing. I need a new spectacular thing.' No, the spectacular thing is a conduit for you to stand on your own two feet."

He mentioned having to cut 15-minute monologues without wrestling on TV for months at a time while he was working part-time and how tough of a task that was, but he accepted and embraced that challenge because it forced him to get creative and be better as a performer.

How generational wrestlers like Gunther handle the peaks and valleys of pushes heating up and dying down will define their legacies and cement their spots atop the totem pole. Gunther not being a permanent fixture in the main event mix at the moment doesn't necessarily mean he won't be world champion again eventually.

"[Gunther's] story is not done," Cena asserted. "I think he's in that position right now where he's making moves based on the equity of Gunther. And sometimes you don't get a dance partner that's equal or greater to you. Sometimes you don't get a 25-year veteran like AJ Styles to make him retire. Sometimes you don't get to retire John Cena. Sometimes you got to lift up younger talent. Sometimes you got to hold the show by yourself.

"Man, matches I'm most proud of are having a beer with the audience in WrestleMania and then getting squashed by The Undertaker, because I felt really good about orchestrating a storyline that could bring back The Deadman as The Deadman," he continued. "I don't know, man. I hope that each performer reaches their potential and, man, that's my hope. I guess that's also the origin story for the opportunistic nature of the John Cena Classic. I just want to get folks out there to have an ability to do their thing the best they can do it."

Whether he's honing his craft in acting or dominating the Clash of Clans world, John Cena will forever have a place in pro wrestling, and although he's still navigating the waters of what in-ring retirement looks like for him, his attitude toward the industry may ultimately make him as invaluable of an asset to WWE outside of the squared circle as he was inside of it.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Predictions for Cody Rhodes, Oba Femi, WWE Sunday Night's Main Event Match Card
articles.summary: This weekend will feature an edition of Sunday Night's Main Event that feels more like a PLE than a TV special based on how it has been booked.
articles.body:
This weekend will feature an edition of Sunday Night's Main Event that feels more like a PLE than a TV special based on how it has been booked.

We will get a dose of celebrity wrestling when Lil Yachty attempts to survive five minutes against Baron Corbin in an effort to earn Trick Williams a shot at the U.S. title.

Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, and their new friend Tatum Paxley, will take on Jade Cargill, B-Fab and Michin in a six-woman tag match.

The two biggest bouts on the card are major grudge matches. Randy Orton will battle Cody Rhodes, and Bron Breakker will step into the ring with Oba Femi.

Let's take a look at each match and make some predictions.

Flair, Bliss and Paxley vs. Cargill and The Baddies

The six-woman tag match is probably the easiest outcome to predict for one simple reason.

Paxley is just getting her feet wet on the main roster, and management is going to want to get her off to a good start, so having her be the one to score the win for her team seems like the most logical outcome.

There are no titles or major stakes in this match, so B-Fab or Michin will likely eat the pin so Cargill can remain protected.

It's going to be interesting to see how Paxley is factored into the women's division once she is on her own.

If Lil Yachty can survive for five minutes against Corbin, then Williams will earn a rematch for the United States Championship.

On paper, this should be a one-sided fight that ends with Corbin crushing the non-fighter, but that is not how things work in WWE.

This is going to be a match with some comedy to stretch out the time, and there is little doubt in anyone's mind that Yachty will last the full five minutes to earn Trick a title shot.

We're definitely going to see Yachty's commitment to bumping tested here, but it could be fun if he is willing to put in as much effort as past celebrity wrestlers like Bad Bunny.

Prediction: Yachty survives five minutes

When Orton fought Rhodes in their last encounter, he came up short because the title was on the line and The American Nightmare was still a top priority.

Now that Rhodes no longer has a belt, he can afford to take some losses now and then. He no longer needs that plot armor the world title brings.

The Viper could use an important victory to help him get back on track toward title No. 15. A win over his former best friend would do exactly that.

The only way this ends without Orton winning is if someone like Kevin Owens gets involved for some reason, but he has bigger fish to fry at the moment.

Breakker and Femi have been earmarked as the future of WWE for quite some time, and they will finally step into the ring for a singles match on Sunday.

They may share some similarities, but their paths couldn't be any different. Femi is a self-made Superstar who impressed WWE and worked his way up the ladder quickly. Breakker, on the other hand, is a legacy as a member of the Steiner family, but his skills and accolades are no less impressive due to his lineage.

This is the hardest outcome to predict because there are a few ways WWE could go with it. It could have either man win cleanly; Breakker could win thanks to interference from The Vision; or it could be The Vision who accidentally cost him the match, creating a rift in the group.

It has seemed like Breakker has had one foot out the door with the group for a while, so this would be an easy way to facilitate that, and for that reason, we are going with Femi to win as a result of Austin Theory and Logan Paul messing something up.

articles.title: Ranking the Top 10 Sports Cinderellas of All Time
articles.summary: The Indiana Hoosiers entered the 2025 college football season with a level of expectation unseen across their decades of futility. articles.body:
The Indiana Hoosiers entered the 2025 college football season with a level of expectation unseen across their decades of futility. But even after they finished 11-2 in their first year under head coach Curt Cignetti in 2024, a national championship run still felt out of reach. After all, they entered the season as +10000 to win the title, well behind preseason favorite Ohio State (+450).

By the time the Hoosiers wrapped up a 13-0 regular season, it was clear that college football's biggest Cinderella story in years had transformed into the nation's most dominant team. Three victories later, it was official.

However, Indiana's unforeseen rise was far from the biggest Cinderella story in sports history. Take a look at where that Hoosiers team ranks among the top Cinderellas ever.

2005-06 Edmonton Oilers 2011-12 Los Angeles Kings 2018-19 St. Louis Blues

Greece (Euro 2004) Emma Raducanu (2011 U.S. Open Tennis)

The Setup: In March 2001, Drew Bledsoe signed a 10-year, $103 million extension with the New England Patriots, which made him one of the NFL's highest-paid players. Despite his status as one of the league's top quarterbacks, the Patriots had still finished 5-11 in 2000, and it looked like things might hit rock bottom when Bledsoe suffered a life-threatening internal chest injury during a Week 2 loss the following season.

The Cinderella Run: With Bledsoe sidelined indefinitely, the Patriots turned to 24-year-old Tom Brady to take over at quarterback. Brady was just one year removed from being a sixth-round pick in the 2000 draft.

In hindsight, it was the start of an all-time great legacy, but the Patriots had been +7000 to win the Super Bowl even with their Pro Bowl quarterback. Now they were turning to a complete unknown.

Brady went 11-3 as a starter in Bledsoe's absence, and the Patriots capped off their improbable run as 14-point underdogs against the "Greatest Show on Turf" St. Louis Rams in Super Bowl XXXVI. They won 20-17 on an Adam Vinatieri field goal as time expired to cement an all-time Cinderella run.

9. 2021-22 Saint Peter's Peacocks (Men's College Basketball)

The Setup: With an enrollment of around 3,000 students and a home attendance average of 546 fans during the regular season, Saint Peter's was the classic automatic-bid afterthought heading into the 2022 NCAA tournament. In fact, they didn't even win the MAAC regular-season title. They finished second to Rick Pitino's Iona squad while going 19-11.

The Cinderella Run: The Peacocks were the talk of the opening round when they upset blue-blood Kentucky in overtime as a No. 15 seed. Mustachioed guard Doug Edert became an immediate internet sensation after pouring in 20 points off the bench.

That alone would have ranked as one of the biggest upsets in tournament history, but Saint Peter's added victories over No. 7 seed Murray State and No. 3 seed Purdue to become the first No. 15 seed to reach the Elite Eight. The Peacocks ultimately fell to North Carolina in that round, but a great Cinderella story doesn't always have to end with confetti and a shiny trophy.

The Peacocks proved that during the 2022 NCAA tournament.

First look at Pro Bowler coaching for CFB team

8. 2025 Indiana Hoosiers (College Football)

The Setup: The Indiana Hoosiers had the most losses of any college football program in history when Curt Cignetti took over as head coach prior to the 2024 season. They had never had a 10-win campaign. They had not won an outright Big Ten title since 1945. They had a losing record in 14 of their last 16 seasons.

Even after vaulting to an 11-2 record in Cignetti's first year on the job, they were still 100-to-1 to win the national championship heading into 2025.

The Cinderella Run: After a 5-0 start in which they outscored the opposition by a 239-48 margin, the Hoosiers were still just No. 7 in the AP poll heading into a high-profile road game against No. 3 Oregon. A 30-20 win in that game galvanized them as a legitimate title contender.

By season's end, they were the first 16-0 team since the 1894 Yale Bulldogs after beating Ohio State in the Big Ten championship and Alabama, Oregon and Miami in the College Football Playoff. Quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman Trophy on the strength of a 3,535-yard, 41-touchdown campaign, and Cignetti had completed one of the greatest turnarounds in sports history.

The Setup: The St. Louis Rams went 4-12 during the 1998 season and had not finished with a winning record since 1989. There was some optimism heading into the 1999 season when quarterback Trent Green joined the team on a four-year, $17.5 million deal in free agency, but that was quickly snuffed out when he suffered a torn ACL in the preseason.

They were +15000 to win the Super Bowl when Week 1 arrived.

The Cinderella Run: In some ways, the 1999 Rams are the NFL equivalent of the 2025 Indiana Hoosiers. They started the season as long-shot title contenders but ultimately morphed into a juggernaut once they got rolling.

Quarterback Kurt Warner, who had never started an NFL game, emerged from obscurity to win MVP while throwing for 4,353 yards and 41 touchdowns. A high-powered offense dubbed "The Greatest Show on Turf" that also included Marshall Faulk, Torry Holt and Isaac Bruce led them to a 13-3 record during the regular season.

The Rams finished the job in a 23-16 thriller over the Tennessee Titans in Super Bowl XXXIV.

The Setup: The New York Mets lost 120 games in their expansion season in 1962 and averaged 108 losses over their first six years as a franchise. They took a modest step forward to a 73-89 record in 1968, but they still finished ninth out of 10 teams in the NL standings.

Young pitchers Tom Seaver, Jerry Koosman and Nolan Ryan provided hope for the future, but they entered 1969 still viewed as being several years away from viable championship contention.

The Cinderella Run: A 62-51 record on Aug. 13 represented a massive leap forward for the Mets, but that still left them 10 games behind the Chicago Cubs in the NL East race.

They went 38-11 the rest of the way, sprinting past a collapsing Cubs team to finish 100-62 and win the NL East by eight games. The "Miracle Mets" swept the Atlanta Braves in the NLCS and needed just five games to defeat a loaded Baltimore Orioles team that would win it all the following year in the World Series.

5. 1982-83 NC State Wolfpack (Men's College Basketball)

The Setup: With a 17-10 record during the regular season, NC State likely would have been on the outside looking in for a spot in the 1983 NCAA tournament had they not secured an automatic bid by running the table in the ACC tournament.

That included an overtime victory against No. 5-ranked North Carolina and Michael Jordan in the semifinals and an 81-78 win against No. 2-ranked Virginia and three-time National Player of the Year Ralph Sampson in the title game.

The Cinderella Run: Even with their impressive run through the ACC tournament, the Wolfpack still had to settle for a No. 6 seed in March Madness. The "Cardiac Pack" would trail in the final minutes of seven different games during their postseason run, including overtime in their first-round matchup with Pepperdine.

They were significant underdogs in the championship game against No. 1 Houston and the famed "Phi Slama Jama" squad led by Hakeem Olajuwon and Clyde Drexler, but came away with a 54-52 victory. The image of Lorenzo Charles dunking home the last-second buzzer-beater and head coach Jimmy Valvano sprinting around the court in celebration will play during every March Madness for eternity.

The Setup: The AFL and NFL announced a planned merger on June 6, 1966, but the two leagues would continue to play separate schedules until the 1970 season when they fully unified. To bridge the gap, the Super Bowl was created to crown a champion at the end of the year.

After decisive victories by the Green Bay Packers in Super Bowl I (35-10) and Super Bowl II (33-14), the AFL quickly earned a reputation as the inferior league.

The Cinderella Run: The New York Jets were multi-touchdown underdogs heading into Super Bowl III against the Baltimore Colts when quarterback Joe Namath famously declared: "We're gonna win the game. I guarantee it."

Then "Broadway Joe" delivered, with some help from a defense that recorded four interceptions, and the Jets came away with an improbable 16-7 victory. The AFL was legitimized, and the impending merger reshaped the NFL forever.

3. 1984-85 Villanova Wildcats (Men's College Basketball)

The Setup: In the first year of the expanded 64-team NCAA tournament format, the 1984-85 Villanova Wildcats slipped into the field as a No. 8 seed. They went 19-10 during the regular season to finish fourth in a loaded Big East, but they went a combined 0-5 against conference heavyweights Georgetown and St. John's.

The Cinderella Run: The Wildcats won their first three NCAA tournament games by a combined nine points, including a 59-55 upset of No. 1 seed Michigan, before upending Brad Daugherty, Kenny Smith and North Carolina to reach the Final Four.

The upsets kept coming with a 52-45 win against No. 2 seed Memphis to set up a national championship game showdown with conference rival Georgetown and star Patrick Ewing. The Wildcats played their best game of the season on the biggest stage, shooting 22-of-28 from the floor and missing just one shot after halftime.

With its 66-64 victory, Villanova remains the lowest-seeded team ever to win the NCAA tournament.

2. 2015-16 Leicester City (Premier League)

The Setup: Leicester City returned to the Premier League for the 2014-15 season after a 10-year hiatus, but they spent much of the season hovering around the relegation cut line.

A late surge helped them finish 14th in the standings, but there was little reason for future optimism. They entered the 2015-16 season as staggering 5,000-to-1 long shots to win the Premier League.

The Cinderella Run: With a 13-1-6 start to the season, Leicester City became the first team in Premier League history to be in last place on Christmas one year and first place on Christmas the following year.

Led by Jamie Vardy (24 goals, 11-match goal streak), they maintained that unexpected hot start into the new year. And on May 2, 2016, they officially completed one of the most unlikely Cinderella runs in sports history by clinching the Premier League title.

Note: Leicester City's stunning Cinderella run was also No. 1 on B/R's "Ranking the Greatest Sports Turnarounds This Century" article, which can be read in its entirety here .

The Setup: With an average age of under 22 years old and a roster made up of amateur and collegiate players, the U.S. men's hockey team was largely an afterthought heading into the 1980 Olympics.

They had finished fifth at the 1976 Games, while the powerhouse Soviet Union was seeking its fifth straight gold medal. A lopsided 10-3 win for the USSR in an exhibition against the U.S. just days before the Olympics further highlighted the perceived gap.

The Cinderella Run: Playing on home ice in Lake Placid, New York, the Americans opened with a 2-2 tie against Sweden before winning four straight to advance to the final round along with Sweden, Finland and the heavily favored Soviet Union.

Playing against the backdrop of the Cold War, the U.S. team trailed 3-2 heading into the third period. Mark Johnson tied things up with his second goal of the game on a power play before Mike Eruzione completed perhaps the most unlikely upset in U.S. sports history with the game-winning goal.

A victory over Finland two days later secured the gold medal, but it's the upset of the Soviet Union that will forever be remembered as the "Miracle on Ice" thanks to Al Michaels' famous call: "Do you believe in miracles? YES!"

articles.title: Sixers legend Moses Malone ranked No. 6 center in history of the NBA
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers legend Moses Malone comes in ranked as the No. 6 center in the history of the NBA.
articles.body:
Moses Malone was the missing piece to a championship puzzle for the Philadelphia 76ers . After coming up just short in the finals in the past, the Sixers signed Malone in free agency 1982 and he immediately made an impact.

Malone won MVP in the 1982-83 season as he averaged 24.5 points, 15.3 rebounds, and 2.0 blocks. He then teamed up with Julius Erving to lead the Sixers to a championship as they swept the Los Angeles Lakers on his way to winning finals MVP.

HoopsHype ranked the top 20 centers in the history of the NBA and Malone comes in ranked No. 6 on the list:

Perhaps the most underappreciated superstar ever, Moses Malone was as dominant as it gets at the center spot with physical toughness as a rebounder, leading the league in nightly boards an astounding six times, including once at 17.6 rebounds per game. Malone was also a monster scorer in the paint, using his brute strength to batter smaller foes down low. Many consider Malone the greatest offensive rebounder the league has ever seen, as his timing and instincts to chase boards on offense were second to none.

All in all, Malone averaged 20.3 points and 12.3 rebounds in his 21 years playing basketball. His first two years were in the ABA with the Utah Stars and then the Spirits of St. Louis before joining the Buffalo Braves in the NBA. He won three MVP awards during his days in the league.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton makes feelings towards Brewers crystal clear after first pitch drama
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers will have some extra motivation heading into their matchup with the Chicago Cubs, as Tyrese Haliburton is set to throw out the ceremoni...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers will have some extra motivation heading into their matchup with the Chicago Cubs, as Tyrese Haliburton is set to throw out the ceremonial first pitch for Milwaukee's opponent. The Pacers point guard had previously received an invitation from the Brewers to handle the honor, only for the team to withdraw it after Indiana eliminated the Milwaukee Bucks in the playoffs.

Haliburton now appears ready to make the Brewers regret pulling that invitation, taking the opportunity to throw out the first pitch for their division rival instead.

Tyrese Haliburton's history with the Milwaukee Brewers

"I was a Brewers fan and then I was supposed to throw the first pitch last summer, and they X'ed that after the playoff series," Haliburton remarked via Fieldhouse Files Scott Agness.

"So I said, 'You know what? I'm no longer a Brewers fan.'"

Haliburton's connection to the Brewers goes back to his childhood in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, where he grew up supporting his hometown team. That loyalty disappeared following the Pacers' playoff victory over the Bucks. Haliburton later joked on The Pat McAfee Show that he was no longer very welcome in Wisconsin. With the Cubs giving him another chance to take the mound, he apparently saw no reason to pass it up.

"Whatever they need me to do, I'll be prepared," the Pacers star guard commented. "I've been working on my pitch. My form is not the greatest, but we've been working on it."

Haliburton proved to be the lucky charm for the Cubs, as Chicago edged the Brewers 2 – 1 at Wrigley Field to split the four game series.

articles.title: Greg Schiano won’t survive this embarrassing Rutgers loss without a miracle | Politi
articles.summary: This was the worst loss in Greg Schiano's 18 years at Rutgers, and it likely will cost the head coach his job.
articles.body:
Greg Schiano is toast. The long, painful slog to the end of his second go-around as Rutgers football coach began on Thursday night with the kind of defeat that seemed stolen from the early days of his first stint.

His Scarlet Knights were outclassed in every way imaginable by an undermanned team from New England that arrived in New Jersey as 28.5-point underdogs. Back when the coach's hair was still jet black, the names on the front of the jersey were UConn and New Hampshire. Now, with his temples speckled with gray, it was Massachusetts.

This one won't soon be forgotten. This one is easily the worst loss in Schiano's 208 career games in Piscataway. But don't stop there. This is worse than any result Chris Ash had in his three-plus years, far worse than any defeat that Kyle Flood suffered, and rivals the worst losses of the long-forgotten Terry Shea years.

Hey, at least back then, Rutgers was barely trying.

Rutgers officials believed these type of days were over. Just a few hours earlier, athletic director Keli Zinn had met reporters in what was an optimistic scrum about the state of her department and its fundraising efforts to support its coaches. She wouldn't say how many victories Schiano needed to keep his job for another season, but her mandate was crystal clear .

"Greg and I are on the exact same page with this: I want what he wants and he wants what I want," Zinn said. "And what that is, in its simplest form, is to improve what we saw from last year."

At 9:23 p.m., after a three-score loss to a UMass team that went 0-12 last season, the question seemed something else entirely. Would Schiano even make it to the end of his 18th season? If you think that's a ridiculous notion, chances are you weren't watching this debacle. Zinn watched every minute.

"Do we have to do this now?" Todd Knisley, a deputy AD who arrived last summer from greener pastures at Ohio State, interrupted when I tried to approach Zinn on the sideline to ask if this loss changed her calculations on the football coach she inherited a year ago.

The short answer, Todd? No. But, after Thursday night, it's hard to envision a scenario in which Zinn isn't having conversations about Schiano's future with all the important people around Rutgers very, very soon.

The obstacle, of course, is money. Schiano is owed $17.4 million on his contract. Factor in whatever it costs to buy out his staff, hire his replacement and fund a better roster, and you're looking at an $80-to-$90-million investment. Rutgers had an $78-million athletic spending deficit last season.

The math is in Schiano's favor. He'll also have 11 chances to emerge from the coffin — Undertaker-style — and a win over a premier Big Ten foe might hold the pitchforks at bay. But let's be real. If the Scarlet Knights look like this against UMass, how will they compete against Indiana, Southern Cal and Michigan?

And this was no flukey loss. UMass pushed Rutgers around on both sides of the ball for three excruciating hours. The Minutemen, who hadn't beaten an FBS team in 34 months — and that was Army — rattled off 24 straight points in the first half like they were the ones paying $1.5 million for the easy W to start the season.

"I've been part of some really tough ones," Schiano said at his postgame press conference. "It's easy to talk about 'chop' when things are going well and it's a great little picture for people, but 'chop' is now. Chop is in adversity and we're smack dab in the middle of it as a team and a staff and I fully believe that they will and I will chop our way right out of this."

Yes, of course, he fell back on the trusty old chop. Yes, of course, he said he was out-coached. Yes, of course, he promised that the "good people" in the Rutgers locker room would rebound. He leaned on all the tired platitudes he has used dozens of times before. But then again, what else could he say?

This was supposed to be the year that Schiano finally had the resources he needed to build a roster that would compete in the Big Ten. Zinn found him that money — a roster payroll that she confirmed to be between $20-$30 million — with the expectation that Rutgers would improve on its 5-7 finish a year ago.

Schiano spent most of the offseason trying to pin that team's failure on the defensive coordinator he demoted midseason. Robb Smith was an easy scapegoat, and when Schiano went out and plucked Travis Johansen from the FCS level, the improved coaching was supposed to solve most of this team's problems.

Well, on Thursday night, it sure looked like this was a personnel problem. Schiano stocked his defense with players from the Citadel, South Dakota and Drake, and in their FBS debut, they looked like players from the Citadel, South Dakota and Drake. It was hard to identify a single difference maker on that side of the ball.

And the offense was a bigger disappointment.

Schiano presumably had the resources to find a starting-quality quarterback, and instead, landed on Boston College transfer Dylan Lonergan. Lonergan, fresh off a 2-10 season at Boston College, threw three interceptions in a performance that made investments in two future NFL skill players — receiver KJ Duff and running back Antwan Raymond — feel like putting a moonroof on an '86 Honda Civic.

"This is the first game of a long year," Duff told reporters after catching nine passes for 196 yards and three touchdowns. "We know that's not us."

Rutgers plays at Boston College next week. Lonergan, who was pulled due to an injury late in the game, is likely to start against his old team if he's healthy. BC, at 2-10, was nearly as bad as UMass last year, so the Scarlet Knights will be favored on the road.

If they lose, all bets are off. Zinn and Rutgers president William Tate likely thought they would have had a few months to plot their strategy on how to handle a poor season.

Now, that timetable has accelerated significantly.

Chants of "FIRE SCHIANO!" rang out from a few of the remaining fans in the fourth quarter three days before Labor Day. How low can this program go? Better question: How long will this head coach last?

articles.title: Five things Wisconsin Badgers football fans must know about Notre Dame
articles.summary: Coming off a year where the Wisconsin Badgers had the most difficult schedule in the nation, they're tasked with playing Notre Dame in Week 1.
articles.body:
Coming off a year where the Wisconsin Badgers had the most difficult schedule in the nation, they're tasked with playing Notre Dame in Week 1.

The Fighting Irish open the 2026 season as the No. 4-ranked team in the AP Poll and the No. 5-ranked team in the US LBM Coaches Poll .

This will likely be the biggest test the Badgers face all year, and it's set to take place at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI.

It may not be a true road game for Wisconsin, but it still serves as a crucial moment for head coach Luke Fickell, someone who's struggled to get anything going with this Badgers program since taking over at the end of the 2022 season.

Heading into Sunday's matchup, Badgers Wire's Jordon Lawrenz had a chance to speak with Fighting Irish Wire's Michael Chen.

In your opinion, is it National Championship or bust for Notre Dame?

It very much seems like that is the case, as the expectations for the Irish are higher than they have been in quite a long time, even surpassing the CFP run in 2024. Returning tons of starters and a quarterback that is in the Heisman conversation will do that. However, it's so difficult to win a title, even without ending the title drought that dates back to 1988, making a deep run in the playoffs will be a successful season, even if the fan base isn't happy about it.

There's been a lot of talk regarding quarterback CJ Carr, but what do you think of the team's running back room heading into the 2026 season?

Aneyas Williams couldn't play due to a pair of stars in Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price ahead of him, but that doesn't mean he isn't a very good back. He had the highest average yards-per-carry on the team last fall, and scores virtually every eight touches he gets. Williams will be a solid lead, but the question is who is behind him. Nolan James and Kedren Young barely have any playing experience, but have talent. It might not matter with how good the Notre Dame line is, though, so at this moment, I have confidence this group can get the job done.

I'm going to get straight to the point with this question... just how good is cornerback Leonard Moore?

Elite. Generational. Moore is on virtually every preseason All-American list, and rightfully so. I'm not sure if [Luke] Fickell is telling the truth saying that he isn't afraid to challenge him, as it could go south very quickly. I think he's the best corner in college football, and should be a top pick in the NFL draft.

When looking at your schedule, where does Wisconsin rank among the most difficult opponents the Fighting Irish will face?

I'd say Wisconsin is in the second tier, as they're a solid team, but not one with tons of expectations this fall. BYU and Miami are clearly better than the Badgers, but Notre Dame won't take the game lightly. They are well aware of the early-season issues that Freeman has had, and want to put that behind them. I think they'll come out with urgency.

Early on, this will be a tussle, as both teams get their feet wet in the 2026 season. As the game goes on, Notre Dame's exceptional depth will show, as they'll be able to rotate different players in without much drop-off in play. Cohesion will play a factor as well, considering how many transfers the Badgers brought in, and how little the Irish did. In the end, Notre Dame will pull away with a solid win. Notre Dame 35, Wisconsin 17.
