articles.title: Oregon State defense preps for stiff test in season opener at Houston
articles.summary: Oregon State football opens its season with a 9 a.m. Pacific kickoff Saturday, Sept. 5 at No. 24 Houston.
articles.body:
The Beavers open the 2026 college football season with a visit to No. 24 Houston , booked for 9 a.m. Pacific Sept. 5 in Texas. Head coach JaMarcus Shephard will take the helm for the first time with Oregon State as a new era of Pac-12 Conference football, and Beavers football, kicks off.

Over the past several weeks, Shephard has named sophomore Braden Atkinson the starting quarterback , raved about the wide receivers and tight ends and elaborated on the system he now has running in Corvallis.

On the defensive side of the ball, one key quality has been standing out above the rest: communication.

"Our defense getting better with communication, that is a massive part of what this game is. From the sideline to the first man then on to everybody else, that's what a lot of people have issues with in week one," Shephard said. "There's communication issues, then you get busted, then guys are open down the field. We have to do an elite job of communicating to our players all throughout the game and we've gotten better at that as camp has gone on."

Oregon State defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said he'll be up in the booth this season for visual purposes, leaning into the overarching communication-driven philosophy.

The pair have collaborated as much as any two coaches can, Shephard said. They've developed a scheme that is organized, functional and allows players the opportunity to rely on their muscle memory and execute with conviction.

"We'll continue to build our foundation on defensive scheme," Shephard said. "That gives our players the ability to go out there and play fast. The communication that comes from the linebacker room will be paramount throughout this game in order for us to be able to do that."

Oregon State linebackers Dylan Lane, Aiden Sullivan, Raesjon Davis and Jabari Odoemenem will play the marquee roles in the defense's communication, linking the backfield to the trenches and keeping a grasp on a dangerous, high-octane Houston offense.

Houston starting quarterback Connor Weigman presents a problem for Oregon State in its preparation.

He's 6-foot-3, 210 pounds, a fifth-year senior and on nearly every quarterback watch list nationwide. A year ago, he was one of four quarterbacks in the NCAA who posted 25-plus passing touchdowns and 10-plus rushing touchdowns — he delivered as one of the most powerful running signal-callers.

Oregon State has been preparing to play against a quarterback with such versatility and athleticism.

"He's a tough dude, he's a tough son of a gun," Shephard said. "He runs the ball tough, he makes people miss, he tries to run people over. That galvanizes your team. When (quarterbacks) run and drop their shoulder into somebody and stand up and they're excited about the game, guess what … the team usually gets excited."

Shephard said to prepare for Weigman, the Beavers made their practice quarterbacks essentially live all week. That means hitting, wrapping and untraining the brain to let up on the QB.

"We tried to get that mindset out of our players that they couldn't touch the quarterback," Shephard said.

MacIntyre and the Oregon State defensive staff have known about Weigman's strengths and have been planning accordingly.

"He is a tough runner. It's not like he's just scrambling around and making plays, which he does that too, but he's downhill, they're running power, they're running counter … he's a physical runner," MacIntyre said. "The thing we have to do is get an extra guy there and make sure when they're pulling people, we have everybody in their right fits because it's basically going to make you have to end up making a one-on-one tackle."

Weigman isn't the only player high on the Beavers' radar, though.

Oregon State's WR1 from 2025, Trent Walker, is now a Houston Cougar.

He's a senior transfer who spebt the last five years at Oregon State. In 2025, he posted over 800 receiving yards, a team high, and two touchdowns. For his career he garnered 1,790 receiving yards and four touchdowns.

Walker hails from Beaverton and is about to step foot inside Reser Stadium for the first time as an opponent. Shephard said he hopes the current Beavers display emotional intelligence when going up against Walker.

"There is a part of going against a former teammate that emotionally gets you going in a way," Shephard said. "We can't be worried about Trent Walker. We're going to worry about what he does on the football field as it pertains to the scheme that they're going to display at Houston. We should have the same emotion about their quarterback, their left guard, their running backs, about those two safeties that are really good players … we should have the same emotional response to those guys that we have to Trent Walker."

MacIntyre shared his perspective on facing Walker.

"They're so used to (transfers) now, it's very common. I don't think they think anything of it, to be honest. Of course you had friends that you roomed with and stuff like that," MacIntyre said. "It's not that framework anymore, it's completely changed."

Houston runs a strong crop of wide receivers including Walker, as well as junior Koby Young and senior all-Big 12 first-teamer Amare Thomas.

That room with Weigman in the pocket presents quite the challenge for the new-look Beavers, but one they are eager to face head on come Saturday.

Oregon State football versus Houston will air on ESPN at 9 a.m. PT Saturday, Sept. 5 from TDECU Stadium in Houston.

ESPN announced the game will also air on Disney+ for subscribers.

articles.title: Shilo Sanders punched a Bills TE. Then he put a different one on his rap album cover
articles.summary: Shilo Sanders altered a photo punching a Bills player for his album cover, replacing Zach Davidson with Dalton Kincaid.
articles.body:
Shilo Sanders thinks he went out swinging. His album cover was a swing and a miss.

The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers safety commemorated the punch that got him ejected against the Buffalo Bills last year on the cover of his new rap album.

Sanders' version of events comes with a remix: He's punching the wrong tight end on the album cover.

Sanders actually threw the punch at Zach Davidson. The player on the receiving end on Sanders' album is Dalton Kincaid.

Kincaid wasn't involved in the confrontation.

It's unclear if the photo was modified using AI, Photoshop or Microsoft Paint.

Sanders and Davidson got into a scuffle away from the play during the second quarter of Buffalo's preseason finale against Tampa Bay on Aug. 23, 2025. Davidson continued blocking Sanders downfield and eventually grabbed Sanders near the left side of his head.

Sanders responded by punching Davidson in the helmet and was immediately flagged and ejected.

"I was just chasing a far-deep DB and trying to finish through the whistle and he had a little bit more to say," Davidson said after the game. "I didn't say anything. I may have gestured something but if you get mad for getting blocked, I can't really control what else he does."

Davidson couldn't control what Sanders did next. Apparently he couldn't control who Sanders remembered doing it to, either.

articles.title: Robinson to judge new Aberdeen side '15 games in'
articles.summary: Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson says it would be "crazy" to judge his new-look side so early in the Scottish Premiership season.  The Dons have been dealt...
articles.body:
Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson says it would be "crazy" to judge his new-look side so early in the Scottish Premiership season.

The Dons have been dealt a tough hand in their opening quartet of league fixtures, a sequence that included games against the top three teams from last term – Celtic, Hearts and Rangers.

After beating Hearts in their opening game, the Dons lost at Dundee before sustaining defeats by both halves of the Old Firm.

Speaking before Saturday's league visit of Kilmarnock, Robinson said: "There are very, very few games been played in the season so far, so to be that judgemental that early on is crazy.

"I will judge the team when we are 15 games in and then what we need and where we go from there.

"We have been tested very, very hard early on with the fixture list, with a new group still trying to bond. We weren't quite up to that test if the truth be told, we weren't quite up to it in terms of results, some of the bits were good.

"But, we will get better and better as it goes."

Robinson added the mood in the dressing room remains positive as they look to end a run of three straight league defeats.

"There is still a belief, there has to be a realism as well," he explained. "We have been beaten by Celtic 3-0, we lost to a penalty against Rangers. If you look at the millions and millions that has been spent on those two squads, we haven't had the luxury to do that.

"I am very, very confident in the group we have put together to have a good season."

Aberdeen will be hoping to get back on the victory trail against a Killie side who have lost all four of their opening Premiership games.

And Robinson added: "There is pressure every time you play at home for Aberdeen to win games, you are expected to win so it is no different to any other game for me.

"It is important to win the game whatever way we do it."

articles.title: Orioles news: Adley’s revenge game continues O’s slide
articles.summary: The Orioles’ longtime catcher returned to Baltimore with a two-homer game for the Red Sox.
articles.body:
Well, gang, the vibes are…not great. The Orioles finally returned to Camden Yards last night after nearly two weeks on the road, but what could've been an uplifting series-opening victory against the Red Sox turned sour in the late innings. There were plenty of reasons for the O's loss, which I'll get to momentarily, but the biggest factor was that Adley Rutschman did Adley Rutschman things, only this time against the Orioles instead of for them.

It was an emotional night for Orioles fans as the Birds' former #1 overall pick and franchise cornerstone played his first game in Baltimore as a member of the opposing team. Rutschman received a loud, extended standing ovation before his first at-bat in the top of the first, and another one after the inning when the Orioles played a tribute video on the Jumbotron. Adley was noticeably appreciative of the crowd, doffing his helmet and holding his hand to his heart, and his greetings with his former teammates were no less joyful (Pete Alonso gave him a hug in his first at-bat, aw).

And then Rutschman went out and beat the Birds , hitting not one but two home runs off an otherwise dominant Brandon Young and setting the stage for Boston's late comeback. Ugh. Talk about a bittersweet reunion. Personally I was hoping we could see Adley succeed but his team fail miserably. We only got the first part of that.

Seeing Rutschman stomp the Orioles just opens old wounds about Mike Elias's decision to trade him. On a baseball level, it made sense, and the O's did get a nice haul of prospects. But man, I wish the Orioles, not the Sox, could be the team that's locked into a playoff spot right now, with Adley helping to lead them to victory. But of course, that would have required the Orioles to put together a more competent team around him.

Last night's loss laid bare the many problems that plague the Orioles right now. Their bullpen has collapsed, with almost no reliever proving to be a reliable option at the moment. Even Yennier Cano, who's been the best of the lot for most of the season, fumbled yesterday by coughing up the go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth. Before that, the O's had a chance to get out of the inning on a double play, but Blaze Alexander spiked the relay throw to keep the Sox alive. So, yeah, bad defense is still an issue for the Orioles, too.

First-year manager Craig Albernaz continues to befuddle everyone with his inexplicable in-game tactics. Last night he astoundingly let Carlos Narváez hit for himself with two on and two out in a tie game in the seventh. Why even have three catchers on the roster if you're not going to pinch-hit for Narváez in such a crucial situation? Samuel Basallo, Jackson Holliday, Heston Kjerstad, and Colton Cowser were all available on the bench, and while the Sox did have a southpaw on the mound, I'd take my chances with any of those left-handed hitters (or Yohel Pozo, if you insist on a righty) instead of Narváez, who is 5-for-55 as an Oriole and has a .486 OPS against lefties this year. Compounding the blunder, Albernaz did pinch-hit for both Coby Mayo and Luis Robert Jr., two far better hitters than Narváez, just one inning later. What are we doing here, buddy?

Overall, the Orioles just seemed fatigued, which is understandable considering their brutal travel schedule of late. Since Aug. 25, they've traveled to the Central Time Zone (St. Louis) to the Pacific (Sacramento) to the Mountain (Denver) and back to the Eastern (Baltimore), all without a single day off. The schedule makers did the O's no favors, and the Birds may be paying the price.

That's the third loss in a row for the Orioles, who remain 1.5 games behind the losing Guardians for the third wild card spot, but have now fallen a full game behind both the Rangers and Blue Jays. The O's have yet to win since Colton Cowser's game-saving catch in Colorado on Monday. I was hoping we'd eventually look at that play as the moment that sparked the Orioles into a playoff run. Instead, we might eventually look at that play as the last time we felt good about the Orioles this season.

That feeling is going to last for more than one night, I think. There are still three more games in this series for Adley to hit a bunch more home runs.

There's a Jim Mora quote that perfectly sums up my response to this headline.

Is today your birthday? Happy birthday! Former Orioles born on this day include catcher Mark Kolozsvary (31), infielder Luis López (56), right-hander Doyle Alexander (76), and the late first baseman Eddie Waitkus (b. 1919, d. 1972).

On this date in 1957, Orioles 18-year-old right-hander Jerry Walker threw a 10-inning shutout to beat the Senators, 1-0. What were you doing at age 18?

In 1969, the Orioles pulled off a ninth-inning comeback in Detroit in most impressive fashion. Down by three runs, they led off the ninth with three consecutive homers by Frank Robinson, Boog Powell, and Brooks Robinson to tie the game. Later in the inning, a Mark Belanger RBI groundout sealed the Birds' 5-4 come-from-behind win.

Exactly a year later, Brooks Robinson contributed to another O's win by going 5-for-5 with two home runs at Fenway Park to top the Red Sox, 8-6. Brooks loved hitting on Sept. 4, apparently.

In 1982, 36-year-old right-hander Jim Palmer threw a one-hit shutout to beat the Twins, 3-0. (And at twice Jerry Walker's age!) It was Palmer's 11th consecutive victory, improving his record to 13-3.

And on this day in 2012, the Orioles demolished the Blue Jays in Toronto, 12-0, behind an 18-hit explosion and Zack Britton's seven shutout innings. The win pulled the O's into a first-place tie with the Yankees, marking the first time in 15 years that the Orioles had been in first place in September.

On Sept. 4, 2018, the Orioles…actually won a game! That's a season where they finished 47-115, so it's a legitimate surprise to discover a win on any given date. The O's beat the Mariners in Seattle, 5-3, thanks to a four-run rally in the seventh. Reñato Nunez tied the game with a homer and Jonathan Villar, Joey Rickard, and Trey Mancini each collected an RBI in the frame. Even Chris Davis, well into his late-career collapse by then, contributed an RBI single in the ninth. Alex Cobb threw a quality start to run his record to 5-15, and Mychal Givens notched the last five outs for the save. The win "improved" the Orioles to 41-98. It snapped a four-game losing streak, though they started a six-game skid the next day.

articles.title: Southlake Carroll vs North Crowley: How to watch Texas high school football
articles.summary: North Crowley hosts Southlake Carroll in a key Texas battle. Here is how to watch the game, plus team breakdowns.
articles.body:
Texas high school football returned last week with some thrilling games.

Week 2 of the season in the Lone Star State shows no signs of the excitement slowing down, as several big matchups dominate the slate of games from Thursday to Saturday.

That includes Class 6A teams North Crowley and Southlake Carroll squaring off for the first time since 2021. Both teams are coming off impressive Week 1 wins, though both of them did it in very different styles.

The Panthers earned a dominant shutout win, while the Dragons needed to mount a comeback to pull off their victory.

If you can't make it to Fort Worth on Friday evening, here's everything you need to know about both teams and how you can watch the showdown from home.

When is Southlake Carroll vs North Crowley high school football game?

The matchup between Southlake Carroll and North Crowley kicks off on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026 .

What time does Southlake Carroll vs North Crowley high school football game start?

The game is slated to begin at 7:00 p.m. CT.

Watch Southlake Carroll vs North Crowley high school football game live

Southlake Carroll and North Crowley fans can watch the game live on the NFHS Network .

Southlake Carroll football: What to know

Quarterback Hudson Tomcheck and wide receiver Brody Knowles helped guide Southlake Carroll from a 27-0 deficit to a 34-33 season-opening victory.

Tomcheck completed 19 of 24 passes for 322 yards with two touchdowns, while also adding two rushing scores for Southlake Carroll. Knowles had seven catches for 180 yards and two touchdowns

In the last matchup between these two programs, Southlake Carroll earned a 42-20 win over North Crowley in the Class 6A Bi-District Playoff Round on Nov. 12, 2021.

North Crowley limited Aledo to negative-10 rushing yards on 40 carries in its dominant 26-0 win to open the 2026 season last weekend. That marked the first time Aledo was shut out since 2003.

Sophomore Braylen Cunningham had a 65-yard pick-six in the dominant defensive display for North Crowley.

Senior Jacob Torres returned to the starting QB position last week in the season opener after missing the 2025 season because he was deemed ineligible. He finished with 189 yards and three touchdowns in his return.

articles.title: FIW staff picks Notre Dame vs. Wisconsin and top Week 1 games
articles.summary: The staff at Fighting Irish Wire pick the winner of Notre Dame vs. Wisconsin along with the top games of Week 1 in college football.
articles.body:
Notre Dame football will get its season started this weekend , but will have to wait for most teams to play before seeing the field themselves.

The Irish start off with the Shamrock Series game, against Wisconsin in Lambeau Field, which may or may not be an advantage for the "home" team. Luckily Notre Dame travels well, its a long weekend also so many fans well head up North for the 2026 opener.

There is plenty on the line for Notre Dame, mostly a trip to the College Football Playoff, and starting the season off on the right foot will be a step in that direction. First, we'll see a decent slate of Week 1 games, as the staff here at Fighting Irish Wire of Tim Healey, Sunny Verma, Kevin Smith and Michael Chen make their predictions for the best games of the real opening weekend along with how they each see Notre Dame's contest against Wisconsin turning out.

Boise State Broncos at No. 2 Oregon Ducks

Date: Sat., Sept. 5th, 2026 at 2:30 p.m. CDT on CBS

Healey - Ducks in a walk. Boise State can be frisky, but Oregon is a true national title contender.

Verma - Oregon wins soundly. Dan Lanning knows the last three national champions have been from the Big Ten, pressure is on the Ducks to be the fourth.

Smith - Ducks by a country mile. Boise State will have a solid team, but there's no doubting the talent that Oregon has this season.

Chen - Boise State's glory days are over, and they're still a solid program, but Oregon is a title contender and they'll show it on Saturday.

Date: Sat. Sept. 5th, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. CDT on ABC

Healey - I wouldn't be shocked if an unranked Clemson stuns the Tigers, and LSU could be a candidate for underachievement this year. Then again, LSU is home. Bayou Bengals in a close one.

Verma - I'm taking Clemson only because it would be one of the greatest days in the history of social media if Lane Kiffin lost after all the drama he's been causing.

Smith - This might be a hot take but with all of the noise in and around LSU at the moment, I don't see the team being focused enough to win this game. I'll take Clemson.

Chen - Every year there is a team that's unranked that makes a run and it could be Clemson this season. They always recruit well, and there's some turmoil at LSU. The visiting Tigers upset the host Tigers.

No. 24 Louisville Cardinals at No. 9 Ole Miss Rebels

Date: Sun., Sept. 6th at 6:30 p.m. CDT on ABC

Healey - Louisville can be a thorn in the side of higher-ranked teams, but I don't see them getting past Ole Miss.

Verma - I think Louisville head coach Jeff Brohm is one of ten best coaches in America. But I don't think he can pull off this upset on the road. Ole Miss wins.

Smith - Those Pete Golding-led Rebels were fun to watch in the CFP last year, so I think that'll continue this season. Ole Miss will take this one.

Chen - Ole Miss has a roster that will compete for a conference title in the SEC, while Louisville will be a tier-1 ACC team, but probably won't win the conference. The Rebels start their season off in a big way.

No. 19 SMU Mustangs at Florida State Seminoles

Date: Mon., Sept. 7th at 6:30 pm. CDT on ESPN

Healey - SMU should be able to handle business here.

Verma - Absolutely nobody was impressed with what FSU showed in Week 0. I don't know if they're going to be that bad all season but I think SMU should be able to handle them.

Smith - FSU is off to a good start, but SMU should have this one without a problem.

Chen - With a Notre Dame interest in mind, we want SMU to win and stay ranked. Florida State hasn't found its groove again, and loses at home.

See photos from Notre Dame football practice on August 7, 2026

Wisconsin is probably good enough to upset Notre Dame, and the crowd will likely be on the Badgers' side, but I think a focused Notre Dame team that still stings from last year's playoff snub should come out on top. I do think Wisconsin will keep it close through three quarters before the Irish lock it down. Figure this one to end with a score that makes the game look closer than it was. Something like 24-14 Notre Dame.

The Badgers will be better than previous years (they almost have to be with the amount they invested in this year's roster) but I don't think they are going to put up much of a fight in Lambeau Field. CJ Carr introduces himself to the general public when it comes to the Heisman picture and Leonard Moore returns a pick-six in a 31-7 Notre Dame victory.

The Badgers are talented this year and I don't doubt they'll give the Irish a game, but Notre Dame seems to be another level of determination this season. With last year's CFP snub fueling Notre Dame, I can see the team pulling off a 31-17 win over Wisconsin.

Opening games have been tricky for Marcus Freeman, and the hope is that he's learned his lesson and the Irish can move past this. Wisconsin's roster is now filled with new transfers and recruits, a good portion of the team is new and that could spell trouble. Notre Dame teaks this one, but not as convincingly as we'd all like, 35-17.

articles.title: Broncos GM provides update on injured tight end’s recovery
articles.summary: The Broncos placed TE Caleb Lohner on short-term IR this week. It could be a few months before he returns.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos must really like tight end Caleb Lohner. Lohner, a second-year player who was a seventh-round selection in the 2025 NFL draft, was placed on the short-term injured reserve list when the club set its 53-man roster on Sunday.

Lohner spent all of 2025 on Denver's practice squad, developing into a football player. Prior to 2024, Lohner mostly made his name as a college basketball player at BYU, the University of Utah and Baylor. Earlier this spring at rookie minicamp, Lohner appeared as an eligible first-year player , and surprised coaches with his transformation.

"He looks entirely different in this camp," Broncos coach Sean Payton said of Lohner in mid-May. "One year into the program, and how he's moving, what he's doing, everything looks entirely different. That learning curve and growth curve was greater for someone who had far less experience, maybe, than others, if that makes sense. It's entirely noticeable, and he's in great shape. You see his athleticism."

Unfortunately for Lohner, shortly after rookie minicamp, he underwent a procedure which kept him off the field during OTAs, minicamp and all of training camp. General manager George Paton gave an update on Lohner's condition on Sunday after the Broncos finished their 53-man roster.

"He's looked good," Paton said. "He was having a really good offseason and obviously had a setback with the foot. We expect him, I'm not sure the timetable, mid-season, maybe. Don't hold me to that."

So we don't have an exact timeline for Lohner's return, but Paton is clearly impressed with the tight end.

"He has all the traits: the size, he can run, he has great ball skills being a basketball player," Paton said. "This would have been a really important preseason and training camp for him. He just needs reps. We're still excited about him. He's here every day working, but we won't see him until late October or so."

Depending on how his rehabilitation goes, Lohner may get his first NFL snaps in 2026. We'll just have to wait and see.

articles.title: Tuioti vs. Tuioti. Oregon, Boise State set stage for family battle
articles.summary: After family playbook leak nearly two decades ago, Tony Tuioti isn’t taking chances when he coaches against his son, Mana, a Boise State linebacker.
articles.body:
The last time Oregon defensive line coach Tony Tuioti coached against a family member, it didn't start the best.

Serving as the defensive coordinator at Silverado High in Las Vegas, Tuioti went head to head with his father-in-law, Paul Nihipali, the offensive coordinator for Chaparral, in the playoffs.

Tuioti said they didn't talk throughout the week. But his defense, which held teams in single-digit scoring throughout most of the regular season, gave up several scores in the first half, alone.

Silverado and Tuioti ended up winning the game, but he found out later that his wife gave his father-in-law his playbook.

See photos from Oregon football's past run ins with Boise State

Fast forward to 2026 and Tuioti, with over two decades of coaching experience, will coach his son, Teitum, who plays edge for the Ducks , this weekend alongside his oldest, Teivis, who is also on the Ducks ' coaching staff. On the other sideline will be his youngest son, Teimana, or Mana, for short, a sophomore linebacker for Boise State .

Don't expect Mana to get Oregon's playbook headed into this weekend, though.

Boise State coach Spencer Danielson joked at the beginning of the week that he instructed Mana to not speak with his dad, but the two have been chatting.

"Yeah, we definitely been talking," Tony Tuioti said. "You know, just really, dad-son conversation, how things are going. But you know, at the end of the day, I already know he's going to come out and he's going to do the best he can with what he's been asked to do on his team and vice versa at the same time."

The Tuiotis moved to Eugene when Tony accepted head coach Dan Lanning's offer to be on his inaugural staff ahead of the 2022 season. Going into Teitum's senior year of high school, Tony asked his son whether he wanted to stay in Nebraska to finish high school or move with the family to Eugene and compete at Sheldon High for one year.

Teitum ultimately chose to move out with his family and finish out a standout prep career in Oregon alongside his younger brother, Mana, who was heading into his sophomore season.

The Tuioti family quickly became a fixture in the Eugene sporting community, and Teitum was one of the best players to ever put on a Sheldon uniform in just one season before enrolling at Oregon a year later.

"Teitum's the best player I've coached," said Sheldon head coach Tyler Martell, then the defensive coordinator. "You have to obviously be physically gifted to do what he's done. But what separates him from other really good players is how hard he practices. That showed up right away."

Led by Teitum and now-Oregon backup QB Brock Thomas, the Irish finished runner-up in the state before Teitum handed the reigns of the Sheldon program to Mana.

Martell said the Tuioti boys he coached brought the same level of preparation and hard work every day, but their temperaments were different. Martell recalls a referee in 2022 striding over to the Sheldon sideline to ask the coaching staff to "do something" about No. 3 (Teitum), who was screaming throughout the game.

The typically playful edge rusher flips a switch when the game starts. The Sheldon coaching staff just shrugged and told the officials he wasn't doing anything illegal, so to just leave him alone.

Mana, meanwhile, while equally as intense, is incredibly cerebral and versatile. Both Teitum and Tony described Mana as smart and a true defensive captain.

Teitum said Mana flipped his own switch in the 2022 state title game against West Linn as a sophomore, in the pair's final game playing together at Sheldon.

"Early on, most of the time he would just listen to me," Teitum said of Mana. "In that state championship, I remember him just flipping a switch. I think he had like 17 tackles, he was very vocal that game. He was telling me where the flow was going and telling me my job. I knew that he would carry on from there big time."

Martell said the Tuiotis quickly became ingrained at the school despite only living here for just under five years.

"They came in and made the Sheldon community part of theirs, with the daughters playing volleyball and the boys playing football for us," Martell said. "And as busy as a guy like Tony is, he always found a way to be in the gym watching his daughters play volleyball, which I think is cool and rare.

"It's really neat to see how they've embraced Eugene and become a part of this community."

The younger Tuioti went on to enjoy his own stellar career at Sheldon before enrolling at Boise State as a linebacker in 2025.

All the while, Mana grew up in high school with Oregon players stopping by the Tuioti house. It'll feel like playing against several of his brothers when Mana steps on the field at Autzen Stadium for the Broncos. Teitum said that there are many Oregon players that consider Mana a brother and are excited to play against him this weekend.

"Matayo (Uiagalelei) would come and see Mana's high school games when he was playing here at Sheldon," Tony said. "Kam Araghi has known Teitum since he was a freshman in high school and Mana was a seventh-grader in middle school. There's a lot of ties that go way back, to see him grow to this point and see him being able to play and contribute to his team makes me really proud as a dad."

Tony said the Tuiotis will be split pretty evenly in terms of blue and green jerseys, and that mom is handling any pre- and postgame connections while Tony, Teitum, Teivis and Mana prepare for the game.

For now, each's entire focus is on winning Saturday afternoon.

"It's one of those things where you want to put pause on life and just enjoy it for a while," Tony said. "But I'm just blessed and grateful that we have this moment, this opportunity, and we're going to enjoy it. This is one of those once-in-a-lifetime situations, and I'm just glad that we get a chance to share it together."

articles.title: How rookie recreates self as fullback to make Miami Dolphins' roster
articles.summary: DJ Herman was a linebacker, but the Miami Dolphins had plenty of them. The undrafted free agent embraced the chance to become a fullback, and just celebrated...
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS — The "unreal" story of the 2026 Miami Dolphins today is standing at his locker, reflecting on the moment his became a nonfiction story.

DJ Herman had been signed by the Dolphins as an undrafted free agent. That was one strike against him.

DJ Herman was a linebacker, but the Dolphins had linebackers . What they didn't have was a fullback. And with coach Jeff Hafley determined to run the ball with De'Von Achane , they wanted a fullback. So not only was Herman asked to change positions, he was asked to move to the other side of the ball. Strike two.

Last weekend was cut-down day in the NFL , the day Herman would find out if his crash course in Fullback 101 resulted in a passing grade, or if it was strike three.

"Sunday was very nerve-wracking," he said. "Waiting all day. No call, which is a good thing. And then from there, 6 o'clock came around and no call. And I found out on social media that I made the 53-man roster, so I'm really happy about that."

Photos of Miami Dolphins 53-man roster - until they add/drop players

It certainly wasn't lost on Herman, this road less traveled he'd taken.

"It's unreal," he said. "It's a real experience, but it's just a great feeling."

Cut-down day couldn't have turned out better for Herman's family. Everyone had gathered to celebrate his sister's birthday, hoping that bad news wouldn't crash the party. Then again, DJ never took the request from general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan to move to offense as one that was going to dent his chances of making the team.

"All you need is an opportunity," he said. "And Sully game me an opportunity."

Jaylen Wright sees some Alec Ingold in DJ Herman

Here was a player being asked to step into a role formerly filled by Alec Ingold, a Pro Bowl fullback. So consider the weight of running back Jaylen Wright attesting to Herman's ability to create running lanes.

"I see Alec in him," Wright said. "Kind of like his mindset, skillset. Just how he goes about his day. He's a pro already."

"The Hermanator," as Herman has been called, is a weekend away from making his NFL debut. Dolphins players have a three-day weekend before Week 1. Some are returning to their alma mater for a game. Some are heading home to visit relatives. Herman?

"Just staying here and doing a lot more film and studying and getting ready for Vegas," he said, referring to the Sept. 13 opener at the Raiders.

Coach Jeff Hafley already appreciates what it took for Herman to get up to speed on the position.

"Everybody thinks of a fullback is you just need a guy who's going to run through the A gap and try to light up a Mike linebacker," Hafley said. "But that guy's got to have the body control and lateral movement and the ability to adjust, which is similar to a linebacker, if you could picture a linebacker moving and tracking a back.

"I give him a lot of credit. He worked really hard to study the new position, the physicality, the toughness, how hard he's worked, and he earned a spot on the team. And that is a cool story."

Herman, 24, is 6-feet-1, 242 pounds and out of San Diego State, where he played linebacker. But the Dolphins stockpiled linebackers in the draft, selecting Jacob Rodriguez, Trey Moore and Kyle Louis. Shortly thereafter came the call Herman didn't see coming.

"They were like, 'Yeah, we're really heavy in the linebacker room, so how about you switch over to fullback and we can get you an opportunity?' " Herman said. "And I'm like, 'Yeah. Let's do it.' "

Herman's prep for the move included studying film of Ingold, coupling what he learned with the body control Hafley referred to.

"One thing is knowing your assignment and just going 100 miles an hour, doing your assignment the right way," he said.

Not every NFL team has a fullback. Herman is grateful he's on one that values it.

"Right now for the Miami Dolphins , fullback is a position to be," he said. "And we're keeping that alive, in my eyes. And when it comes to the team and what we need to do for the offense, the fullback needs to be in there and get the job done."

articles.title: How rookie recreates self as fullback to make Miami Dolphins' roster
articles.summary: DJ Herman was a linebacker, but the Miami Dolphins had plenty of them. The undrafted free agent embraced the chance to become a fullback, and just celebrated...
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS — The "unreal" story of the 2026 Miami Dolphins today is standing at his locker, reflecting on the moment his became a nonfiction story.

DJ Herman had been signed by the Dolphins as an undrafted free agent. That was one strike against him.

DJ Herman was a linebacker, but the Dolphins had linebackers . What they didn't have was a fullback. And with coach Jeff Hafley determined to run the ball with De'Von Achane , they wanted a fullback. So not only was Herman asked to change positions, he was asked to move to the other side of the ball. Strike two.

Last weekend was cut-down day in the NFL , the day Herman would find out if his crash course in Fullback 101 resulted in a passing grade, or if it was strike three.

"Sunday was very nerve-wracking," he said. "Waiting all day. No call, which is a good thing. And then from there, 6 o'clock came around and no call. And I found out on social media that I made the 53-man roster, so I'm really happy about that."

Photos of Miami Dolphins 53-man roster - until they add/drop players

It certainly wasn't lost on Herman, this road less traveled he'd taken.

"It's unreal," he said. "It's a real experience, but it's just a great feeling."

Cut-down day couldn't have turned out better for Herman's family. Everyone had gathered to celebrate his sister's birthday, hoping that bad news wouldn't crash the party. Then again, DJ never took the request from general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan to move to offense as one that was going to dent his chances of making the team.

"All you need is an opportunity," he said. "And Sully game me an opportunity."

Jaylen Wright sees some Alec Ingold in DJ Herman

Here was a player being asked to step into a role formerly filled by Alec Ingold, a Pro Bowl fullback. So consider the weight of running back Jaylen Wright attesting to Herman's ability to create running lanes.

"I see Alec in him," Wright said. "Kind of like his mindset, skillset. Just how he goes about his day. He's a pro already."

"The Hermanator," as Herman has been called, is a weekend away from making his NFL debut. Dolphins players have a three-day weekend before Week 1. Some are returning to their alma mater for a game. Some are heading home to visit relatives. Herman?

"Just staying here and doing a lot more film and studying and getting ready for Vegas," he said, referring to the Sept. 13 opener at the Raiders.

Coach Jeff Hafley already appreciates what it took for Herman to get up to speed on the position.

"Everybody thinks of a fullback is you just need a guy who's going to run through the A gap and try to light up a Mike linebacker," Hafley said. "But that guy's got to have the body control and lateral movement and the ability to adjust, which is similar to a linebacker, if you could picture a linebacker moving and tracking a back.

"I give him a lot of credit. He worked really hard to study the new position, the physicality, the toughness, how hard he's worked, and he earned a spot on the team. And that is a cool story."

Herman, 24, is 6-feet-1, 242 pounds and out of San Diego State, where he played linebacker. But the Dolphins stockpiled linebackers in the draft, selecting Jacob Rodriguez, Trey Moore and Kyle Louis. Shortly thereafter came the call Herman didn't see coming.

"They were like, 'Yeah, we're really heavy in the linebacker room, so how about you switch over to fullback and we can get you an opportunity?' " Herman said. "And I'm like, 'Yeah. Let's do it.' "

Herman's prep for the move included studying film of Ingold, coupling what he learned with the body control Hafley referred to.

"One thing is knowing your assignment and just going 100 miles an hour, doing your assignment the right way," he said.

Not every NFL team has a fullback. Herman is grateful he's on one that values it.

"Right now for the Miami Dolphins , fullback is a position to be," he said. "And we're keeping that alive, in my eyes. And when it comes to the team and what we need to do for the offense, the fullback needs to be in there and get the job done."

First, though, he has to win a job he never expected to be chasing.

The Dolphins had a gap in their roster. And this rookie just hit it.

articles.title: Reds sign St-Etienne teenager N'Guessan for £4.3m
articles.summary: Liverpool have completed a £4.3m deal for French forward Djylian N'Guessan from St-Etienne.  The 18-year-old will spend the first half of this season on loan...
articles.body:
Liverpool have completed a £4.3m deal for French forward Djylian N'Guessan from St-Etienne.

The 18-year-old will spend the first half of this season on loan at Ligue 1 side Brest, officially joining the Reds in January, when his situation will be reviewed.

N'Guessan is a product of the St-Etienne academy. He made his debut in January 2025 and featured 13 times, scoring one goal. St-Etienne have a sell-on clause in the deal with Liverpool.

As with goalkeeper Lucca Brughmanns, who was signed on transfer deadline day in a deal that could be worth up to £30m , the move for N'Guessan is a result of work from Liverpool's global talent department that is led by Matt Newberry.

The forward featured seven times for France at the 2025 U20 World Cup and was also named in the team of the tournament at last summer's U17 European Championship.

Earlier this year, the Reds signed Senegal's Mor Talla N'diaye and Austria's Ifeanyi Ndukwe after the teenage centre-backs both impressed at the U17 World Cup in Qatar, while goalkeeper Armin Pecsi and midfielder Samuel Martinez have both joined in the past 12 months from Hungary and Colombia, respectively.

articles.title: Five reasons why Auburn football will beat Baylor in Week 1
articles.summary: Auburn football set to take on the Baylor Bears on Saturday in Atlanta and here are five reasons it will be a victory for the Tigers.
articles.body:
Game one of Alex Golesh's era is set to begin on Saturday against the Baylor Bears in the Aflac Kickoff Game in Atlanta, Georgia.

Earlier this week, we examined five factors that could cause Auburn to struggle against the Bears . Today, we will have a more optimistic outlook on the game.

Though Auburn is in a rebuild year under new head coach Alex Golesh, game one still should heavily favor the Auburn Tigers on Saturday against the Baylor Bears. This has not been your typical rebuild in college football because the Tigers brought in an impressive transfer portal class, with quarterback Byrum Brown being the headliner.

The resources that Auburn athletics has make it an easier process to get back to a competitive program in the SEC compared to other national programs. The missing piece is just a head coach, a man to go in and guide the program in the right way. That is something they did not have in the Hugh Freeze era and definitely not in the Bryan Harsin era.

Photos: Auburn's 2025 win over Baylor on the road

Because of Golesh, many on the Plains have hope in this year's Tigers. Hope is a dangerous thing for SEC fans, but honestly there are plenty of reasons to have hope. Golesh is as real as it gets as a head coach in college football, not one to answer with coach speak. That personality trait showed up in the offseason in recruiting as the Tigers lit it up in June, landing multiple four-star recruits.

This weekend we get to now see the coaching side, most important part, of Golesh with his Tiger squad heading to Atlanta to take on the Bears in the Aflac Kickoff Game. Here are five reasons why Auburn and Alex Golesh will walk away with a win against Baylor.

Let's start with the biggest reason and factor in the game that leans in the Tigers' favor. The quarterback play has been lackluster on the Plains since Bo Nix departed after the 2021 season. Now the Tigers have a guy in Byrum Brown, who makes it when the Tigers stack up against opponents where the quarterback is the stronger piece. Brown is a playmaker and a game changer. He finished last season leading the country in total touchdowns with 42. He will make the plays when Auburn needs it and will be a difference-maker all season long.

It's a new year in Waco, Texas, on defense, and the Bears need a refresh after an awful defense that they fielded in 2025. Last season, Baylor allowed nearly 400 yards a game and also made former Auburn quarterback Jackson Arnold look amazing. Baylor brought in a new defensive coordinator, Joe Klanderman, to clean up that side of the ball. It's not going to be a quick turnaround for the Bears' defense. Golesh is going to flex his offensive genius against this defense.

DJ Lagway's turnover issues may not be resolved

Baylor brings in transfer Florida quarterback DJ Lagway. He's been a player with a ton of expectations, expectations that have not been met. Coming out of his freshman year, many in the media touted him as potentially the best quarterback in the SEC. Well, 14 interceptions; he is out at Florida, and he lands in Waco. I think his confidence took a hit, and I think it continues to decline going up against a top SEC defense in Auburn. Expect him to get careless with the ball late in the game.

This room is stacked. You have the main starter Jeremiah Cobb, who should probably finish with 1,000 yards this season. Behind him are two starting caliber players in Omar Mabson II and Bryson Washington. This is where Auburn will control the clock and the pace of the ball game with effective running from this running back room that is deep.

Auburn is an SEC team, and with that comes SEC talent. I know SEC bias is a real thing, but this is a Big 12 team that wasn't great last season and lost key players like Sawyer Robertson. Auburn added players like Cody Sigler and DeShaun Womack on defense. The Tigers retain Xavier Atkins and Elijah Melendez, who will be causing nightmares for DJ Lagway in Atlanta all day.

articles.title: 5 storylines for Ohio State vs. Ball State Saturday | Buckeyes Wire
articles.summary: Ohio State football kicks off it season on Saturday when it hosts Ball State in the 'Shoe. Here are five storylines to watch in Game 1 of 2026.
articles.body:
The long college football offseason is over, and that means YOUR Ohio State Buckeyes will be back in action to open the 2026 season against Ball State inside the venerable Horseshoe.

Each season is a new one with different players, coaches, and identity, and that will be the case with this year as well. From new turf to new on-field seats , to a lot of new players, and even a new offensive coordinator , there's a lot to unwrap with this scarlet and gray gift we're about to see Saturday.

Each game within a season makes its own mark as well, so we like to look ahead with some storylines before the Buckeyes go and do battle on the gridiron each week. Ohio State is highly favored in this one, but there's plenty to keep an eye on over this perceived speed bump, so let's dig in.

Here are five storylines to watch when Ohio State takes on Ball State Saturday afternoon.

What impact will new Ohio State O-Coordinator Arthur Smith have?

Smith brings an NFL scheme and mindset to Columbus, much the way defensive coordinator Matt Patricia did last season. There's a palpable buzz coming out of the Woody Hayes Athletic Center about the difference Smith has made with scheme, effort, and culture.

Look for multiple sets for plays, creative ways to get the best players the ball, and a little use of mismatches and tempo at times, among other things. More than anything, I'm anxious to see how varied the window-dressing and creative sets are during the game Saturday.

How good is Ohio State QB Julian Sayin 2.0?

The Ohio State quarterback had a fantastic first year as a starter, leading the nation in accuracy and finding his way to New York as a Heisman finalist. But that was just his first season as the starter. You would expect the Southern California native to take a step forward in year two, and we've heard that there's been some significant improvement from both the players and the coaches.

From his command to even better accuracy, to how quickly Sayin goes through his reads and gets the ball out of his hands, even head coach Ryan Day has been quick to compliment his development in the spring and fall. The team voted Sayin as one of the captains this year, and I can't wait to see what kind of player he's become with a little extra seasoning.

Has Ohio State RB Bo Jackson improved his game-breaking ability?

One of the biggest things the coaching staff lamented last season was the offensive players' lack of explosiveness after the catch or in the second level of runs. Bo Jackson had one of the best freshman seasons of any running back last season, but he too missed some opportunities with yards after contact, or when in space after getting through the initial defenders.

It was an emphasis by the coaching staff this offseason, and Day has said that Jackson is much better in that department. It's one thing to show it in practice, though; all of Buckeye Nation wants to see it when the bright lights of the games are on, and we should be able to observe a little of that Saturday afternoon.

Is Ohio State WR Devin McCuin as advertised?

Most of us thought that 5-star freshman receiver Chris Henry Jr. would get a chance to be that third starter alongside Jeremiah Smith and Brandon Inniss , but we had to change that mindset with some of the comments Day and the coaching staff have made about UTSA transfer Devin McCuin .

When speaking to the media earlier this week, Day said that many in the building would say that McCuin is as good as anyone they've had at receiver. What? Yes, that's a shocking statement, and if it's true, the Buckeyes are going to have one whale of a receiving corps in 2026, and I can't wait to get my first taste of it this weekend.

Can the Ohio State defense retool at a high level?

It's the big elephant in the room. The Ohio State defense was tops in the country last year, and while that's a good thing, losing so many guys to the NFL is not -- maybe. The Buckeyes have to replace three guys that were drafted in the top 11 of the 2026 NFL draft, and that means we're really going to see if Patricia can earn his pay.

Clearly, there's still some talent left in the cupboard, but can this defense approach the level of last year's, or will there be some growing pains? You have to believe the scheme will be great again, but there's not much time to get things where they need to be with a top-five matchup with Texas looming after this one. Seeing new guys emerge is just the way things are done each year at Ohio State, and hopefully that's the case again in 2026.

articles.summary: Raiders sign former Falcons EDGE to practice squad

The Atlanta Falcons didn't have any major surprises on their initial 53-man roster for 2026, but one player who was somewhat overlooked on cut day was edge rusher Azeez Ojulari. The former second-round pick out of Georgia signed with the Falcons in March to provide edge depth but failed to make the team.

According to a report from ESPN insider Adam Schefter , Ojulari was one of three players - along with wide receiver Ronnie Bell and guard Evan Neal - to sign with the Las Vegas Raiders practice squad on Thursday.

Ojulari didn't have an exceptional training camp in Atlanta by most accounts, but considering Jalon Walker's season-ending ACL injury and James Pearce Jr.'s eight-game suspension, it was somewhat surprising to see the veteran pass rusher passed over for both the 53-man roster and 16-man practice squad.

The 26-year-old recorded eight sacks as a rookie with the New York Giants in 2021, but he hasn't recorded more than six sacks in season since. Ojulari has recorded 113 tackles (61 solo), 22 sacks and 38 QB hits in 49 games (32 starts) over his five NFL seasons (four with the Giants and one with e Philadelphia Eagles ).

Ojulari will join former Falcons QB Kirk Cousins in Las Vegas. Cousins was just named the starter over Fernando Mendoza. articles.title: Florida football position preview: Experience anchors linebacker room
articles.summary: Myles Graham and Aaron Chiles headline a Florida linebacker room that returns nearly all of its 2025 snaps and adds emerging young depth.
articles.body:
Florida returns almost its entire linebacker room from last season, bringing back 1,605 of the 1,641 snaps played at the position in 2025.

Linebackers coach Greg Gasparato has one of the most experienced groups on the roster. Myles Graham, Aaron Chiles and Jaden Robinson all played more than 450 defensive snaps last season, while sophomores Ty Jackson and Myles Johnson have continued to push for larger roles.

The position also carries some added significance under Jon Sumrall, a former linebacker who spent much of his coaching career working directly with the position. Florida's new defensive coordinator Brad White has a 3-4 foundation, but White can change the personnel and responsibilities of the linebackers depending on the package.

Here's a closer look at Florida's linebacker room heading into the 2026 season.

Check out Gators Wire's other position previews:

Starting Linebacker: No. 5 Myles Graham (Jr.)

Graham is the unquestioned leader of the linebacker room after starting all 12 games and leading Florida with 76 tackles last season. He became the first Gators linebacker to lead the team in tackles since 2021 and was one of the most important players Sumrall and Florida's new coaching staff retained during the transition. Graham also helped convince several other key players to remain with the program.

At 6-feet-1-inch and 228 pounds, Graham has developed into a true three-down linebacker. He's at his best playing downhill, earning a 79.0 PFF run-defense grade last season, while also grading well as a tackler and pass rusher. Graham generated 15 pressures on just 56 pass-rush snaps, giving White another way to use the centerpiece of the linebacker room.

"I think we have an ability to play fast, but physical, play downhill," Graham said of the new defense. "I think the d-line will do the same, too, so just making the right play behind them, and zoning up and just creating turnovers. It will help us do that too."

Starting Linebacker: No. 8 Aaron Chiles (Jr.)

Chiles has matured from a rotational player to the other listed starter alongside Graham after appearing in every game last season and recording 52 tackles. He made his first career start against Tennessee, tying his career high with nine tackles in the process.

At 6-feet-3-inches and 238 pounds, Chiles gives Florida a different style of linebacker next to Graham. He primarily played in the box last season, but PFF also charted him with 42 snaps along the defensive line. Chiles can play off the ball, walk toward the line of scrimmage or handle SAM-type responsibilities in heavier packages.

In White's 3-4 scheme, the SAM is the strong-side linebacker, which lets Chiles play closer to the line of scrimmage. He can set the edge against the run, match up with tight ends in man coverage, blitz off the edge and drop into short-zone coverage.

Chiles also leaned out during the offseason and has continued to improve his understanding of coverage, giving Florida even more flexibility with how he's deployed.

"He is big, he's strong," Gasparato said. "I just think he's got a unique skill set and size at 240 pounds where you can use that guy a lot of different ways."

Veteran Rotation: No. 29 Jaden Robinson (Sr.)

Robinson is the most experienced linebacker on Florida's roster, appearing in 37 career games with 17 starts. He started all 12 games last season and finished with 50 tackles, four tackles for loss and two sacks.

The Week 1 two-deep gives Robinson a starting role, but he'll serve as a third linebacker and the first man off the bench when Chiles or Graham need a break. Robinson has experience playing multiple linebacker roles, giving White a veteran option when Florida changes personnel.

One of his best traits is his ability to create pressure as a blitzer, which makes him a natural fit for some of the SAM-style responsibilities in White's defense. PFF credited him with 17 pressures on 56 pass-rush snaps last season, including two sacks and 14 quarterback hurries.

Young Rotation: No. 7 Ty Jackson (So.) and No. 44 Myles Johnson (So.)

Both Jackson and Johnson spent most of their freshman seasons on special teams, but each has claimed a more distinct role in the rotation during the offseason. The Week 1 depth chart lists Johnson directly behind Graham, while Jackson is part of the rotation behind Chiles.

Jackson barely played defensively as a freshman, logging just seven defensive snaps. He appeared in eight games, mostly on special teams. His résumé coming into Florida was impressive: ESPN ranked him as the No. 1 inside linebacker and No. 54 overall player in the 2025 recruiting class after he recorded 391 tackles in 32 high school games.

The athleticism has carried over, but Jackson needed time to adjust to the speed and level of competition in the SEC. He's made significant progress with his awareness, confidence and play recognition, putting himself in position to earn meaningful defensive snaps.

"He's seeing things cleaner," Sumrall said. "His vision lines have improved. He's adjusting better. His spatial awareness has improved. He's always had great athletic traits. Now his football training is elevating."

At 6-feet-2-inches and 228 pounds, Jackson also gives Florida another explosive, downhill option in the middle of the defense.

Johnson appeared in all 12 games as a freshman and played a meaningful role on special teams, even though he played only 17 defensive snaps. Four of his five tackles came in the opener against LIU.

All 17 of Johnson's defensive snaps came in the box, but his special teams workload was much larger. PFF credits him with 60 snaps on kickoff coverage, 46 on kick return and 26 on punt return, giving him plenty of game reps, albeit in a different role.

The sample was tiny, but Johnson earned a 90.1 overall PFF grade across those 17 defensive snaps without missing a tackle. He's listed directly behind Graham entering Week 1, giving him a clear path to a much larger defensive role as a sophomore.

Johnson has also added size without sacrificing speed. He's one of the most athletic linebackers in the room. Gasparato singled him out as one of the biggest risers in the room during spring practice, and Sumrall continued to praise his effort during fall camp.

Bullard, the older brother of walk-on JACK Titus Bullard, transferred to Florida after four seasons at UCF, where nearly all of his playing time came on special teams. He appeared in 26 games for the Knights and recorded four career tackles.

In 2025, PFF charted Bullard for just 22 defensive snaps compared with 101 on special teams, including 38 on kickoff coverage, 36 on kick return and 20 on punt return.

At 6-feet-1-inch and 213 pounds, Bullard gives Florida another experienced special teams option and emergency depth at linebacker. He is listed in the backup rotation behind Chiles entering Week 1 but is more likely to make his biggest impact on coverage and return units.

His family has extensive ties to Florida. His father, Thaddeus Bullard, played defensive end for the Gators before becoming WWE star Titus O'Neil, and his uncle is former Florida running back Earnest Graham.

Morris arrives as another talented developmental option in an already crowded room. ESPN rated the Lakeland product as a four-star recruit, the No. 2 linebacker nationally and No. 179 overall player in the 2026 class.

He was named The Ledger's All-County Defensive Player of the Year in 2024 after recording 95 tackles, nine sacks and three forced fumbles. At 6-feet and 246 pounds, Morris already has the size and physicality to play in the SEC, but Florida's veteran depth should allow the staff to bring him along gradually.

Walk-Ons: No. 42 Matthew Kade (Jr.) and No. 52 Dylan Leighton (So.)

Kade joined Florida as a walk-on in 2024 and has yet to appear in a game. The Gainesville Buchholz product was a high school teammate of Graham and finished his senior season with 90 tackles, 18 tackles for loss and five sacks.

Leighton joined the program as a walk-on in 2025 and also has yet to appear in a game. Both provide additional developmental and practice depth behind an experienced scholarship rotation.

Chicago Bears ' starting running back D'Andre Swift and rookie wideout Rome Odunze got injured during Thursday's final pre-season practice, but medical reports confirmed that Swift only has a minor muscle cramp and is set to play in the Week 1 season opener.

Swift complained of severe abdominal discomfort after a carry from the 1-yard line and left the practice holding his midsection.

A few hours later, ESPN insider Adam Schefter and medical sources clarified that it was just a temporary cramp and he's on the path to a quick recovery. Earlier, receiver Odunze had also limped off the field with the trainers due to a right leg issue.

articles.title: Game 1 Preview: Clemson Travels to Take On LSU
articles.summary: Start of the Rebound or Same as it Ever Was? Greetings STS folks! I’m excited to be back with the game previews for this upcoming football season. Obviously...
articles.body:
Start of the Rebound or Same as it Ever Was?

Greetings STS folks! I'm excited to be back with the game previews for this upcoming football season. Obviously 2025 was not a lot of fun, leading to an understandable level of trepidation coming into this season with a game of this magnitude to kick things off. Game 1 certainly won't make or break this season, especially with it not even being a conference game.

That said, it is past time for Clemson to put a quality performance up against one of the programs receiving a ton of preseason hype (not to mention one of the biggest spenders in the nation for their roster). It is a tremendous opportunity for Dabo Swinney and this program if they can manage to seize the moment after flailing away at these more often than not since 2020. I grew up on old school NWA rasslin', so in the words of the American Dream Dusty Rhodes, "Let's quit talkin' 'bout it! Let's take it to tha rang!"

Clemson Defense vs. LSU Offense: I've had a lot of time to think about this game. The more I ponder it, the more I believe that Clemson has to at least break even on the lines of scrimmage to have a shot in this contest. If that happens, I like Clemson's chances to spring the upset because of the measures the staff has taken to upgrade the deficiencies of the defense in the back. This is without a doubt a much faster and rangier secondary group than what the team has fielded in the last couple of seasons. Last year's group had the bad combination of lack of speed/range and poor assignment details. That made mistakes hurt twice as much because they couldn't make up for them with athletic ability.

Dabo Swinney supported Tom Allen both with portal decisions and staff changes which you have to hope will make a huge difference. The Tigers simply couldn't press enough to eliminate the quick passing games of most teams last season, which was one of the big reasons the touted DL didn't have the type of impact most (including me) felt it would. You have to be able to make the QB hold the ball and work through his progressions to let your pass rush really do its job. Clemson was so good at this during the Venables era and it led to massive sack numbers over those years. Increased speed in the back should allow for more aggressive options versus the quick game, which was a major part of LSU's offensive plan last year and mirrored by most of Clemson's opponents during that terrible start to 2025.

Lane Kiffin and Company are now at LSU, which means his fast-break offense is too. The Tigers must hold up against the quick inside zone runs and occasional counters that he typically uses to set up his deep shots and chunk plays. If Clemson isn't effective on first and second down vs the run game, it will be a very long night even with the upgrades in the secondary. Kiffin brought in Sam Leavitt from Arizona State which gives him a legit dual threat QB to work with. They have plenty of tools to be good on offense, so Clemson's game plan is likely going to be centered on limiting the explosives and being strong inside the 25.

If you go back to the 2019 title game blowout against Alabama, you saw the blueprint for how to deal with that level of high octane offense. Outside of a couple of early big plays Alabama got, they did all their damage between the 30s and then got stoned inside of that. The Tide finished that game with 428 yards and 5.7 yards per play but only 16 points. That was easier to do with the elite DL the Tigers had back then, but conversely LSU won't be as loaded as that Tide team was overall on offense either. Still, it all starts with not getting mashed up front and being sound with tackling.

Clemson's question marks at DT are no secret. The best news about this game is that it's game 1 – the Tigers are as healthy now as they can be and will hopefully get through this game with their top 3 DTs being able to handle the lion's share of the snaps. That isn't a recipe for prolonged success as the season goes, but the time for depth building will come after this trip. If Amare Adams, Markus Strong, and Andy Burburija can stay full go all night, Clemson can hopefully be stout enough. If Clemson loses (and loses big as some have predicted), this spot will be a likely suspect.

Last year's game was lower scoring than most thought it would be. Openers can be tricky because of all the unknowns coming in on both sides due to changes in staff and personnel. However, it is likely LSU will at least score in the 20s and the Clemson Tigers have to hold it there; LSU getting to 30 or more will be very bad news. Turnovers are always a major variable that are hard to predict and can offset some things (especially for an upset-minded team). Clemson got a big one in the first half of last year's game but Ricardo Jones didn't have the speed to score on the return and Clemson was only able to get a FG out of it.

Clemson Offense vs. LSU Defense: Clemson's struggles in openers have been a major story in the post 2020 slide. Offense has been the biggest culprit for the struggles. Clemson has faced some strong defenses, especially that 2021 UGA unit, but at the same time the absolute ineptitude has put too much pressure on the defense and it has wilted in most of these games as a result. Garrett Riley's tenure was wrought with extremely poor execution and performance in the openers. Last year's 10 points was the HIGH mark for scoring in openers during his 3-year run. Chad Morris is back and simply has to re-inject the scoring prowess into the offense. I do believe that is going to happen, but how long it takes is something that is just impossible to know.

Morris' 2011 offense was dynamic but it had its issues through the first two and a half games before taking off in the second quarter against Auburn. Clemson has put a major emphasis on getting the running game back in gear and getting the physicality back to where it needs to be. It is certainly past time for Matt Luke's presence to be felt in a positive way. There were signs in 2024 that it was going to be the case, but last year was a major letdown for a multitude of reasons, including poor OL play. How much of that was a lack of cohesion on the offensive staff and Dabo? We are about to find out because if nothing else, Chad Morris and Dabo are in alignment and that should be reflected down the line the same way misalignment was reflected in 2025. Dabo put his faith in the OL room which Luke has almost entirely recruited at this point. We will probably never know if Luke made a push to sign a portal OL or 2, but the Clemson OL is as important as CV or Tait Reynolds. Clemson has plenty around those guys if the OL can hold up its end of the bargain.

Riley was thoroughly outcoached by LSU's defensive staff in last year's contest. I'll never forget LSU getting its best pass rushers isolated on either RBs or even slot WRs versus OL or TEs. It seemed like Riley's entire gameplan was built on Antonio Williams, and when Williams went out early with the hamstring, the plan went with him. But hopefully that is in the rear view mirror with Morris back in town, who has more than proved he knows how to get multiple weapons activated when he has them in his arsenal. Clemson's ability to keep the run game as a legitimate threat will help limit LSU's ability to be exotic with their pressures. Can Clemson win the explosive play margin and protect the ball? Can Clemson at least match LSU in rushing? If Clemson wins, the answers to those questions will almost certainly be yes. That answer has been a resounding no in all but one opener since 2020.

Mansoor Delane was worth every penny LSU paid to get him last year as he was a major revelation for them at corner and helped them negate Clemson's supposed advantage on the perimeter of last year's contest. Thankfully, Delane is gone to the NFL and you have to hope LSU hasn't got an equivalent in place this week. Clemson needs Bryant Wesco and/or TJ Moore to deliver, especially when LSU gambles with single coverages. CV's lone start had good numbers largely because Moore was such a difference maker for him. Clemson has to break into the 20s at a minimum to win this game and that likely isn't happening if every drive is dink and dunk. Putting any QB in constant third and long situations is a recipe for losing, but even more so with guys who are less proven at this point. I at least am confident that Chad is not scared. My only issues with him during his first tenure at Clemson was his habit of getting impatient and forcing things downfield a little too much at times, never with being too conservative.

Special Teams: Dabo went and brought in Rich Bisaccia to overhaul this phase in a move I felt was long overdue. There was a stretch where Clemson just needed to be OK in special teams because of the dominance in the other phases. Those days are gone, and Clemson needs to get more out of this spot and certainly cannot afford the gaffs that have happened in recent years with protections, kicking, and sometimes covering. I think back to Dabo's first full season in 2009 and how much dynamic special teams play helped that team get to the ACC title game. It certainly helped to have guys like CJ Spiller and Jacoby Ford on the team, but they were also put in a position to dominate.

Clemson has some horses to work with and this new era of college football is closer to NFL in terms of parity across the land than ever before. Getting a boost in this phase could very well be the difference between 7-8 wins or 9-10 wins and beyond. 2009 was probably a 6-7 win squad had special teams not been the factor they were that year. Conversely, last year's team got very little help from this phase and really needed it. We won't really be able to assess Bisaccia's impact until we have multiple games in the books, but it certainly would be terrific if they could produce a big positive on Saturday night. Of course avoiding a disaster is first and foremost. Nolan Hauser needs to be the weapon he has shown he can be with the margins as thin as they have gotten for Clemson. The Tigers finally have an elite speed return option now with CJ Johnson and are long overdue for a big TD return.

Overall: It seems a little foolish to pick Clemson to win this game given the unknowns and recent trends versus opponents like this. It might seem crazy to think good can come from not winning, but if Clemson can just demonstrate it can trade punches with LSU and take this game to the wire, there would be plenty of room for optimism for the season to make the turn the program needs. Can Clemson land the first gut punch or initial big play? That was sorely lacking in 2025 and really many of the games in the last three to four seasons. Last year's game started with what should have been a TFL going for a nearly 20-yard rush for LSU. The 2024 UGA game started with Clemson's offense doing nothing. The 2023 Duke game was a travesty of epic proportions.

I want to see the edge and the fight that we as fans began to take for granted. LSU clearly believes they are going to win and win handily, you can sense it with some of their comments in their pressers. Dabo has played the "bunch of nobodies" card quite a bit on this end. If LSU wins because they just manage to make a couple of more competitive plays, I can live with it as bad as that will hurt. If they win because Clemson keeps helping matters with brain cramps and moments of soft play, then we might be in for another season of hoping for a bowl game. Last year's game was close but it seemed that was LSU managing to suck a little less than Clemson did that night. We all know the difference when we see a real dog fight.

Clemson's difference makers need to be difference makers. The big money guys on this roster need to deliver on that investment. 2025's legacy was a lot of those guys falling short. If I had to pick two I thought truly delivered from the departed group, I would pick Avieon Terrell and Blake Miller. Adam Randall was about as good as could be expected for a guy changing positions. It was a mess behind that with either injuries or disappearing acts in too many games. We've heard all about a closer team and other things that you hope are actually true. There have been plenty of talking heads kicking dirt on the program. Saturday night is an awesome stage to rewrite the narrative. I can't pick a win but I will pick a fight.

Arsenal have received nominations for the Manager and Player of the Month awards, following an encouraging start to the season in August.

Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

The Premier League have announced their nominees for the Manager of the Month and Player of the Month awards for August, with Arsenal receiving nominations in both categories.

Mikel Arteta has been nominated for Manager of the Month, having led Arsenal to two wins and a goal difference of +4 in the Gunners' opening two games of the new campaign.

No other manager can better that, but Enzo Maresca can match it with Manchester City . Though City have conceded twice more than Arsenal, they've also scored twice more.

It's not hard to guess the other two nominees, as they're the managers of the other two clubs to win two from two – Hull City's Sergej Jakirovic and Chelsea's Xabi Alonso . Voting is open here until Monday, September 7th at 12:00 BST.

Then Riccardo Calafiori has been nominated for the Player of the Month award for August.

Calafiori is up against Chelsea duo Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro , Manchester City's Rayan Cherki , Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes , Brentford's Mamadou Sangare , Hull City's Konstantinos Tzolakis , and Newcastle United's Yoane Wissa .

The Premier League write that Calafiori has been nominaed for his two assists and Arsenal's two clean sheets, with the Italian international impressing at left-back. Voting is open here , again until Monday, September 7th at 12:00 BST.

The nominations don't even include the fact that Arteta's team won the Community Shield against Manchester City, nor that Calafiori scored in that game.

Regardless, they are two well-merited nominations for the Arsenal duo, and hopefully there will be more to come in September.
