articles.title: Volleyball: Three takeaways from Legacy's four-set win at John Carroll
articles.summary: Legacy High volleyball improved to 5-0 this season after a four-set victory at John Carroll Catholic on Thursday night.
articles.body:
PORT ST. LUCIE — The John Carroll Catholic and Legacy High volleyball teams decided the District 13-5A championship in one of the most thrilling matches of the 2025 season.

Since the two teams are no longer in the same district, Thursday night's meeting marked their only matchup of the season. The rematch resembled the previous meeting, with the Lions celebrating on the Rams' home court once again.

Legacy cruised in the final two sets, using a pair of massive runs to secure a four-set victory. Set scores were 25-18, 23-25, 25-13 and 25-14 Thursday night at Howard Avril Court.

"I think we maybe lost sight of the little things in the second set. They won some 50-50 balls, and I think a lot of things didn't go our way, but what I was proud of was the way these girls responded," Lions head coach Christy Quigley said. "They didn't let the previous set bother them, and they came out and just played their game."

High school volleyball: John Carroll hosts Legacy

After narrowly dropping the second set, the visitors had their full arsenal on display to pull away. Quigley credited her team's serve-receive play as well as its improvement at the service line. The Lions finished with eight service aces, including three from Lyla Barker-Bray.

When the Rams stayed in system and put together attacks, Legacy tightened up its block and consistently turned them away. The Lions finished with 16 total blocks. Senior middle blocker Bailey Johanson led the way with 10 total blocks, including four of the solo variety.

Legacy used a 10-0 run to create separation in the third set and an 8-1 surge to do the same in the fourth. The Lions closed out the match with a 5-0 run, spearheaded by Johanson, who sealed the victory with three consecutive kills.

Johanson and senior outside hitter Taylor Smith each recorded a team-high 13 kills. Smith was one of five Lions with 10 or more digs and finished with a team-best 14. Senior setter Meredith Prince dished out 39 assists, one shy of her season high.

Improving to 5-0, Legacy joined Vero Beach (4-0) as the Treasure Coast's only unbeaten teams nearly three weeks into the 2026 season. Meanwhile, John Carroll (5-1) suffered its first loss.

"I think we learned about ourselves," Rams coach Dustin Wood said. "Give them credit, they exposed some things, but I don't think we played well at times. They were just a little more consistent, and our youth showed. We had three or four sophomores out there at a time, so our inexperience got us a little bit tonight."

Here are three takeaways from Thursday night.

The Lions made history in their debut season, winning the school's first district championship in any sport and advancing to the regional finals.

Many of the same players are back for 2026.

Johanson, Prince and Smith are team captains, while Barker-Bray returns after leading the team in kills a season ago. Other key returners include senior right-side hitter Sophia Spychalla, senior defensive specialist Kherington Neikirk and junior defensive specialist Paisley Woods.

"I feel like not a lot of teams have the chemistry that we do," Johanson said. "Knowing that you're able to trust the person next to you to do their job, while you're doing yours, definitely builds a strong connection and helps us win a lot of games that can be really difficult."

With the pieces back in place, Johanson believes the Lions can make a run at the state tournament. Quigley echoes those sentiments.

"We'd love to replicate what we did last year, but it's always good to have dreams and goals, to do what we couldn't do last year and get past that last loss," Quigley said. "That's kind of our focus, to get there again and, this time, be stronger and more prepared."

For all of its returners, Legacy has one addition that players and coaches believe could put the team over the top.

Jordyn Johnson joined the roster after playing for Lincoln Park Academy last season. The senior has already made an impact, both on and off the court.

"She's brought a lot of energy, and it sparks our team," Quigley said of Johnson.

For all of their success, the Lions felt the absence of another middle blocker alongside Johanson. The addition of Johnson has seemingly helped solve that issue, and the numbers back it up.

Legacy has averaged 8.1 blocks per match through its first five matches this season. That's up from 4.4 blocks per match in 2025.

"She has been such an amazing force in the middle," Johanson said. "She has great energy, a great attitude and can put a ball down when needed."

John Carroll seeks its third consecutive regional postseason appearance. The team hopes to do so under a new head coach.

Wood is in his first season as the Rams' head coach. He takes over for Bianca Maikranz, who stepped down after guiding the program from 2022-25.

A native of East Petersburg, Pennsylvania, Wood played collegiately at Ohio State and East Stroudsburg before transitioning into coaching, where he has spent most of his career at the collegiate level. He served as both an assistant and head coach with stops at East Stroudsburg, George Mason and, most recently, Georgia Southern, where he was the women's head volleyball coach from 2013-18.

Additionally, Wood has contributed to USA Volleyball, serving as head coach of the USA Boys Youth Select Continental Team.

Wood stepped away from coaching as his family grew. But he decided to return as his daughters began their volleyball careers. In addition to taking over the reins at John Carroll, Wood is the technical director at Vero Elite Volleyball Academy.

"It's one of those things where we just try to give back. I love the game," he said.

The new Rams head coach said his coaching style has not changed in the move to the prep level. He emphasizes relationships while developing his players and teaching the game.

After implementing several new systems, Wood has been pleased with how John Carroll has come together and is optimistic about where the team will be later in the season.

"We're not near where we're going to be at the end of the year. This loss is just a blemish, but we're good," he said.

articles.title: Leeds and Wigan set for 'winner takes all' showdown
articles.summary: Leeds and Wigan are set to meet in what is likely to be a "winner takes all" battle for the League Leaders' Shield at Headingley on Saturday.
articles.body:
Leeds Rhinos and Wigan Warriors are set to meet in what is likely to be a "winner takes all" battle for the League Leaders' Shield at Headingley on Saturday (20:00 BST).

The two sides are both on 40 points from 25 Super League matches, with the Rhinos top on points difference, before the penultimate gameweek of the season.

Victory for Brad Arthur's Leeds would effectively clinch the title as their points difference is already 174 better than Wigan's.

Leeds welcome lowly Hull FC for their final game of the regular season the following week, while the Warriors host Catalans Dragons.

Third-placed Warrington, two points behind the top two, are technically still in the hunt for the Shield but their inferior points difference means they would need a miracle to claim top spot.

Leeds are looking to claim the minor premiership for the first time since a dramatic final-day win at Huddersfield Giants gave them the crown, ahead of Wigan, in 2015.

'It's a Grand Final before a Grand Final'

Matt Peet's Wigan have won their past 13 Super League matches and came out on top 24-4 in the reverse fixture in May.

Arthur said his side are "up for the fight" against the in-form visitors.

"You have your pre-season camp in Tenerife and you talk about these wonderful dreams and things you want to achieve and unfortunately for the majority of teams in the competition those things don't become a reality," he told BBC Radio Leeds.

"I've been there plenty of times before but this is the reality for us now, a winner takes all really.

"I'll maintain it's hard to get there but it's harder to stay there. We're up for the fight."

Arthur is looking for his first piece of silverware with Leeds since taking over in July 2024 and the club's first since the Challenge Cup in 2020.

"We've got a lot of respect for them but we need to focus on ourselves and really go after the occasion," he added.

"The majority of the place will be full of our fans so we've got to make the most of the opportunity. There's no pressure on us, we just need to go after it and enjoy it.

"It's no good getting here, we've got to make the most of it because these opportunities don't come along every year.

"It's a Grand Final before a Grand Final. There's a lot riding on the game but we're just grateful that we're here."

Wigan, meanwhile, are looking to win a second competition this season after lifting the Challenge Cup in May.

They have won two Grand Finals and two League Leaders' Shields in the past four campaigns since Peet took charge but he does not think their big-game experience will be a factor on Saturday.

"I think it's very much whichever team plays well on the night," he told BBC Radio Manchester.

"I don't think winning different trophies in different years counts that much. We've got some experienced players who've played in big games but Leeds have as well."

Sivo could return for Leeds, Nsemba in Wigan squad

Leeds have named returning winger Maika Sivo in their 21-man squad for the match, although Arthur said on Tuesday he is more likely to play against Hull FC the following week.

The 32-year-old Fijian has missed the past five games with a broken arm he suffered in the win over Bradford on 26 July.

He is Super League's leading try scorer this year with 29 from 19 appearances.

Meanwhile, Wigan have included forward Junior Nsemba, who has been out with a hamstring injury since 5 July, in their squad.

Peet said the 22-year-old "will feature" in Saturday's game.

articles.title: 'The tough times have shaped me' - Hume reflects on early retirement
articles.summary: Former Sunderland defender Denver Hume has opened up about the "really tough period" that led to his early retirement from football at 28.  Hume had not play...
articles.body:
Former Sunderland defender Denver Hume has opened up about the "really tough period" that led to his early retirement from football at 28.

Hume had not played since October 2025 after suffering a bleed on the brain during a training session with Fleetwood Town, something then manager Pete Wild said seemed to be "an innocuous collision" at the time.

A product of Sunderland's academy, he made 84 senior appearances for his boyhood club between 2018 and 2022 - the most he made for a team in his career.

"It's been a really tough 11 months since I suffered the injury," Hume told BBC Radio Newcastle.

"There was a lot of uncertainty about it. It was a lot more complex than any other injury. Definitely the goal at the start was to get back playing, but as the months go on and the symptoms persisted, I sat down with doctors. From then, it was looking at the next steps for me."

Despite his traumatic experience, Hume is remaining positive and wants to use his struggles to help others.

"The tough times I went through and the setback I had made me the person I am today," he added.

"Without that, my outlook on football and life would be very different and that's why I have the attitude I have. The tough times have shaped me into who I am and I want to use that to help people in and out of football in their journeys."

Hume also reflected on his 14 years at Sunderland, from boy to man, and the love he still has for the club.

"It was a massive part of my life," he said.

"There are still people at the club I am in touch with. The club being back in the Premier League is brilliant and it's a club I will always follow.

"I still speak to Luke O'Nien. He's a great lad and has done unbelievable for himself. He helped me when I was a younger player at Sunderland and I spoke to him a lot during that point. Massive respect for him and I'm very happy to see him in the Premier League."

articles.title: Lautaro Martínez proud of Barcelona interest but vows to stay at Inter forever: ‘Inter means everything to me’”
articles.summary: Lautaro Martinez has said interest from Barcelona made him proud but outlined his commitment to Inter Milan.Martinez was named as a potential transfer target...
articles.body:
Lautaro Martinez has said interest from Barcelona made him proud but outlined his commitment to Inter Milan .

Martinez was named as a potential transfer target for Barcelona as the Spanish champions sought to sign a centre-forward in the summer window.

Barcelona are understood to have made an approach for Martinez, who has scored 175 goals in 378 games for the Serie A side. The approach was turned down with Inter president Giuseppe Marotta insisting the two-time Capocannoniere winner was not for sale at any price.

Martinez has now opened up on the rumours, and said he intends to end his career at the San Siro.

"'I would stay forever': Lautaro Martinez proud of Barcelona interest but vows loyalty to Inter

"When these offers and calls come in, it is always a pleasure, because you work to stay at the top. The rumours were true, but I am very clear about my ideas: I wanted to stay here with my teammates and with these magnificent fans," Martinez told Sky Italia.

"I would stay forever and, as long as they want me, I will stay here. But in this job we already know how it is: when you are no longer useful, they throw you out.

"Inter means everything to me: pride, happiness, and the desire to keep moving forward. I have chosen to stay here again, I want to do great things at Inter.

"I never imagined reaching this point in my career with Inter, achieving all my goals. This motivates me to keep moving forward; it's my mentality. I try to give my all in every training session.

"In football, you never know what is going to happen, but today I have a contract and I am happy. I decided to stay because I feel good and I want to achieve great things at Inter."

articles.title: El Grupo Volkswagen lo confirma: por primera vez apunta a "una retirada gradual de la marca SEAT"
articles.standfirst: Por primera vez el Grupo Volkswagen habla de la posible desaparición de la marca española, aunque la decisión se tomará en 2030
articles.summary: Por primera vez el Grupo Volkswagen habla de la posible desaparición de la marca española, aunque la decisión se tomará en 2030
articles.body: La dirección del Grupo Vokswagen ha dado un salto cualitativo en sus habituales manifestaciones sobre el futuro de SEAT al poner sobre la mesa, por primera vez, la posibilidad de una "retirada gradual" de la marca española. Lo ha hecho en un comunicado en el que hay mensajes contradictorios, donde se mezclan palabras de apoyo para el presente pero con nubarrones para el futuro... aunque siempre con el contexto de que "no se ha tomado una decisión definitiva" sobre SEAT. "La compalía seguirá con los lanzamientos y la actualización de producto planificada, incluyendo la introducción de las versiones microhíbridas del Ibiza y el Arona prevista para 2027. Más allá del actual ciclo de producto, sin embargo, la dirección futura de la marca SEAT sigue bajo evaluación", se asegura. SEAT tendrá que enfrentar en los próxmios años un escenario complicado para su actual situación, como se reafirma también en la comunicación de la compañía: "En la situación actual, una normativa cada vez más exigente, los aspectos económicos de la electrificación y la inversión necesaria para desarrollar una nueva generación de modelos hacen que la viabilidad económica de seguir invirtiendo en la marca SEAT resulte cada vez más complicada". "Por lo tanto, siguen siendo posibles varios escenarios más allá de 2030. Dependiendo de cómo evolucionen la normativa, la demanda de los clientes y las condiciones del mercado, esto podría incluir una retirada gradual de la marca SEAT. No se ha tomado ninguna decisión definitiva". Ante todos los rumores de las últimas horas, el mismísimo presidente del Grupo Volkswagen, Oliver Blume, se ha manifestado sobre el futuro de la empresa española SEAT SA [que engloba a las dos marcas, SEAT y CUPRA] en estos términos: "SEAT SA tiene un papel fundamental que desempeñar en el futuro del Grupo Volkswagen. La compañía ha demostrado su capacidad de transformación, con una sólida base industrial en Martorell y el notable desarrollo de CUPRA. Me enorgullece lo que el equipo de SEAT y CUPRA ha logrado en los últimos años, y esto me da gran confianza en el futuro", explica el directivo alemán. "Estamos comprometidos a consolidar estas fortalezas y crear las condiciones para que SEAT SA y CUPRA continúen creciendo y contribuyendo al éxito del Grupo. Al mismo tiempo, debemos mantenernos flexibles y adaptar nuestras estrategias de marca y producto a la normativa, las condiciones del mercado y las demandas de nuestros clientes". Es importante matizar que Blume da una visión de futuro sobre SEAT SA (SEAT + CUPRA)... pero sólo se refiere a la marca SEAT de forma individual cuando habla del equipo que trabaja conjuntamente para las dos firmas españolas. Más claras son, en este sentido, las palabras de Matías Carnero, presidente del Comité Intercentros de SEAT S.A. y miembro del Consejo de Supervisión de Volkswagen AG : "SEAT S.A. no es una sola marca. Es una compañía que tiene a SEAT y a CUPRA, una huella industrial estratégica y un papel cada vez más importante dentro del Grupo Volkswagen". Y deja en el aire la posibilidad de cambios importantes en esa estructura bajo la palabra 'transformación: '"La transformación nunca es fácil, pero si trae inversión, más responsabilidad y crecimiento a Martorell, también puede crear nuevas oportunidades para nuestra gente. También el CEO de SEAT, Markus Haupt, se manifestaba en esta misma línea: “SEAT S.A. se está preparando para estos distintos escenarios desde una posición de fortaleza: con una base industrial transformada, un papel cada vez más importante dentro del Grupo Volkswagen, un mayor potencial de crecimiento para CUPRA en Europa y a nivel internacional, y la flexibilidad necesaria para adaptar nuestra estrategia de marca a medida que evoluciona el mercado.”

articles.title: Cherki voted Etihad Player of the Month
articles.summary: Rayan Cherki has been voted the Etihad Player of the Month for August.Our French playmaker saw off the challenges of Josko Gvardiol and Marc Guéhi to win the...
articles.body:
Rayan Cherki has been voted the Etihad Player of the Month for August.

Our French playmaker saw off the challenges of Josko Gvardiol and Marc Guéhi to win the first Club award of the season.

Cherki has enjoyed a stellar start to the 2026/27 campaign.

He kicked off by coming on in the second half of the opening weekend clash with Bournemouth with City 0-1 down at the time.

Two assists later, Cherki had helped turn that deficit into a crucial opening day 2-1 win over the Cherries.

Cherki was then at his sparkling best as he starred in the Blues' 4-1 win away to Crystal Palace, scoring two exquisite goals to keep our 100% start to the season going.

Congratulations to Rayan and thank you to the thousands of supporters who took time to vote.
